definition_zh: 在…下画线；在…下面划线；强调；凸显
definition_en: to draw a line under a word or phrase, or to give special importance to something
core_image: 一支笔在纸上的字句下面压出一道笔直的横线，把这句话从纸面上抬起来
scene: 老师在黑板上写下一串生词，转身提醒全班把最难的那个词划出来。She underlined the word twice so nobody would miss it.
sceneCN: 这里 underline 是「在…下画线」（第 1 个义项：在文字下方画出线条）；句意为她把这个词划了两遍，好让谁都不会漏掉。纸上被划出的那道横线，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「下划线；划线做法」
由同义近形词构成，义为「在…下划线；强调」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「划线的；带下划线的」

senses.title: A line drawn beneath words
senses.definition: to draw a straight line under a word or phrase, usually to mark it as important
senses.definitionCN: 在词或短语下面画一条直线，通常用来标记其重要性
senses.example: She underlined every new word in her notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 她把笔记本里每个生词都划了下划线。
senses.why: The prefix under- puts the line below, and line is the stroke itself; the word is almost a picture of what it does.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 under- 把线放在下面，line 就是那道笔画；这个词几乎把动作画了出来。

senses.title: To stress a point
senses.definition: to give special emphasis to an idea, fact, or statement when speaking or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作时特别强调某个想法、事实或说法
senses.example: The report underlines the need for cleaner water in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 报告强调了这个村子需要更干净的水。
senses.why: An underlined sentence is one the reader must not skip; stressing a point does the same thing with the voice.
senses.whyCN: 划线句是读者不能跳过的一句；强调某点就是用声音做同样的事。

senses.title: A mark of emphasis
senses.definition: a line drawn under written or printed words as a mark of emphasis or of a link
senses.definitionCN: 在书写或印刷文字下方画出的线，用作强调标记或链接标记
senses.example: The teacher put a red underline under the misspelled name.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在拼错的名字下面画了一道红色下划线。
senses.why: The verb became a noun: the stroke itself is now a thing you can see and point at.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成了名词：那道笔画本身成了看得见、指得出的东西。

senses.title: Printed with a line below
senses.definition: printed or displayed with a line beneath the letters, as links and titles often are
senses.definitionCN: 字母下方带有线条地印刷或显示，网页链接与标题常如此
senses.example: In the old dictionary every headword appears underlined in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧词典里，每个词目都以加粗并划下划线的方式出现。
senses.why: Here the word describes the look of the text rather than an act: the line is already there.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词描述的是文字的样子而不是动作：线已经在那里了。

senses.title: To make something stand out
senses.definition: to make a quality, problem, or difference more obvious, as if drawing a line under it
senses.definitionCN: 使某种性质、问题或差别更加明显，如同在其下面画线
senses.example: The empty seats underlined how few people had come.
senses.exampleCN: 空着的座位更凸显出到场的人有多么少。
senses.why: The image moves off the page: whatever is underlined stands out from everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 意象离开了纸面：被划线的东西总是从周围一切中凸显出来。

intro.en: Underline is a plain English compound, made of a preposition and a Latin loanword, and it is recorded only from the modern period.
intro.cn: underline 是朴素的英语复合词，由一个介词与一个拉丁语借词组成，直到近代才有记录。

items.en: The preposition under is native Old English under, meaning beneath or below.
items.cn: 介词 under 是本土的古英语 under，意为「在……之下」。

items.en: The noun linea meant a linen thread used as a plumb line, and from it a drawn line.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 linea 原指铅垂用的麻线，后指画出的线。

items.en: Line entered English through Old French ligne, so the two halves of the compound come from different layers.
items.cn: line 经由古法语 ligne 进入英语，因此这个复合词的两半来自不同层次。

items.en: English joined under and line to name a stroke drawn beneath writing; the verb follows the noun closely.
items.cn: 英语把 under 与 line 合起来，指写在文字下方的一道笔画；动词紧随名词出现。

items.en: Later the word was extended to emphasis in speech and to anything that stands out from its background.
items.cn: 后来这个词被扩展到言语中的强调，以及任何从背景中凸显出来的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words built with under-; the near-meaning group gathers marking and stressing verbs with different tools.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 under- 构成的词；近义组收标记与强调的动词，所用手段各不相同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning hidden beneath the surface but real and important.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「潜在的、根本的」，指藏在表面之下却真实重要。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning at a deeper or more basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「从根本上、在更深层次上」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to weaken something gradually from below.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐削弱、从根基上破坏」。

entries.definition: A noun or verb for the outer edge or a summary; it looks close but means the opposite kind of line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「轮廓、概要」；拼写相近，但指的是另一种线。

entries.definition: A noun for material laid under a carpet or floor covering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衬垫、地毯下面的垫层」。

entries.definition: To give special importance to something in speech or writing; it does not use a visible mark.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调」，用于言语或写作，不依赖可见的标记。

entries.definition: To mark text with colour or to draw attention to the most important part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用彩笔标出、突出」，多指用颜色而非线条。

entries.definition: To say a word or point with extra force, or to place emphasis on it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「强调；重读」，指用更大的力气说出某词或某点。

entries.definition: To make a feature more noticeable; more formal and often about appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使突出、加剧」，较正式，常指外观上的特征。

entries.definition: A general verb for putting a sign on something; underline is one particular kind of mark.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「标记」，泛指做记号；underline 是其中一种具体的标记方式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two plain pieces of the compound and the situations where the word really appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词的两个朴素部件，以及这个词真正出现的场合。

normal.en: under plus line: draw the line under the words.
normal.cn: under 加 line：把线画在字的下方。

normal.en: A teacher says underline it, and the class reaches for a ruler.
normal.cn: 老师说把这个词划出来，全班就去拿尺子。

normal.en: Highlight uses colour, underline uses a stroke.
normal.cn: highlight 用颜色，underline 用笔画。

normal.en: Underlined links are the old look of the web.
normal.cn: 带下划线的链接是网页早年常见的样子。

normal.en: A fact that underlines a problem makes it impossible to overlook.
normal.cn: underline 一个问题，就是让这个问题无法被忽略。

abstract.en: Think of a sheet of paper with one line pressed into it: everything above the line is what you must not miss.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸被压出一道线：线以上的内容就是你绝不能漏掉的部分。

abstract.en: The stroke can leave the paper: a silent empty hall underlines what nobody dared to say.
abstract.cn: 这道笔画可以离开纸面：空荡无声的大厅会强调谁也不敢说出口的话。

abstract.en: To underline is to choose: out of a whole page, one line is singled out to be seen.
abstract.cn: 划线就是选择：整页之中，只有一行被挑出来被看见。

examples.en: Please underline the words you do not know.
examples.cn: 请把你不认识的词划上横线。

examples.en: The mayor underlined that no new taxes would be raised this year.
examples.cn: 市长强调今年不会新增税收。

examples.en: Thin ice round the pond underlines the danger of skating there.
examples.cn: 池塘边薄薄的冰更凸显出在那里滑冰的危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱恩」——安把莱恩的名字在纸下划了一道线：划下划线、强调

root: 由本土介词 under（古英语 under，在下面）与拉丁语 linea（麻线、线，经古法语 ligne 入英语）组成，字面即「在字下画线」，近代英语才合成此词。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of underline all keep one gesture: a stroke placed beneath something so that it stands apart from what surrounds it.
sensesIntro.cn: underline 的五个义项都保留同一个动作：在某物下方画一道笔画，让它从周围脱离出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen draws a straight stroke right beneath a word on the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔在纸上的一个词下方画出笔直的一道线。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the hand draws the line under a word.
branches.cn: 纸面线：手在词的下方画出这条线。

branches.en: THE MARK: the stroke becomes a visible sign, and printed text can carry it already.
branches.cn: 标记线：笔画成为可见的标记，印刷文字也可以自带这道线。

branches.en: THE VOICE: stressing a point does with speech what the line does with ink.
branches.cn: 声音线：强调某点是用言语做这道线用墨水做的事。

branches.en: THE BACKGROUND: what is underlined stands out from everything around it.
branches.cn: 背景线：被划线之物从周围一切中凸显出来。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: from a school exercise to a warning sign, the same downward stroke is repeated.
branches.cn: 动作线：从课堂练习到警示信号，重复的都是同一道向下压的笔画。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: an English preposition plus a Latin noun, with ordinary suffixes for the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个复合词结构透明：一个英语介词加一个拉丁语名词，词族其余成员用普通后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea is recorded and came to English through Old French ligne; only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linea 有文献记录，经古法语 ligne 进入英语；只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: The prefix places the stroke lower than the letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把笔画放在字母的下方。

items.example: The noun names the stroke that gets drawn.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被画出的那道笔画。

items.example: The Latin noun named the mason's cord.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词原指工匠用的麻绳。

items.example: French carried the noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个名词带进英语。

items.example: A close synonym built the same way.
items.exampleCN: 用同样方式构成的近义词。

items.example: The opposite kind of line, around rather than below.
items.exampleCN: 方向相反的另一种线：绕在外面而不是压在下边。

items.example: The word is its own best example.
items.exampleCN: 这个词本身就是自己最好的例子。

latinEntries.structure: Old French noun from Latin linea

definition_zh: 承担；着手做；从事；承诺；保证
definition_en: to accept a task or responsibility and begin to carry it out, or to promise formally that you will do something
core_image: 一个人蹲下身，把倒在地上的重物扛到自己肩上，然后站起来往前走
scene: 工程队接到山区修路的委托，队长在会议室里沉默地看了很久地图。He agreed to undertake the work before the rainy season.
sceneCN: 这里 undertake 是「承担某项工作」（第 1 个义项：接受任务并开始去做）；句意为他在雨季到来之前答应承担这项工程。把重物扛上肩的那个动作，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「任务；事业；承诺」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「承办人；殡葬承办者」
由过去分词转用，义为「已承担的；被承办的」

senses.title: Take a task onto yourself
senses.definition: to accept a piece of work or a duty and start doing it
senses.definitionCN: 接受一项工作或职责并开始去做
senses.example: The firm agreed to undertake the repairs at its own cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司同意自费承担维修工作。
senses.why: Under- is beneath and take is to grasp: you take the load onto yourself and carry it from below.
senses.whyCN: under- 是「在下」，take 是「抓住」：你把重负抓过来搁在自己身上，从下面托着走。

senses.title: Promise to do it
senses.definition: to promise, often in a formal way, that you will do something
senses.definitionCN: 通常以正式方式承诺自己会做某事
senses.example: Both sides undertook to keep the talks secret.
senses.exampleCN: 双方承诺对会谈内容保密。
senses.why: Once a task is taken on, the promise is simply the spoken side of the same act.
senses.whyCN: 任务一旦承担下来，承诺就是这同一个动作说出来的那一面。

senses.title: Carry out a study or inquiry
senses.definition: to begin and carry through an organized activity such as a study, survey, or repair
senses.definitionCN: 开始并完成研究、调查、维修等有组织的活动
senses.example: The team will undertake a full survey of the river next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 团队明年春天将对这条河进行全面调查。
senses.why: Research is heavy work that someone must lift; it is undertaken the way a load is.
senses.whyCN: 研究是一件必须由人抬起的重活，承担它的方式就像扛起一包货物。

senses.title: Formally agree to be responsible
senses.definition: to agree formally to be responsible for a job, especially for payment or delivery
senses.definitionCN: 正式同意对某项工作负责，尤指付款或交付
senses.example: A local builder undertook to finish the bridge by October.
senses.exampleCN: 一家本地建筑商承办了在十月前建成这座桥的任务。
senses.why: This is the legal face of the load: the contract states who has agreed to carry it.
senses.whyCN: 这是重负在法律上的样子：合同写明由谁同意去扛。

senses.title: Set out on a journey
senses.definition: to start on a long journey or a difficult course of action
senses.definitionCN: 开始一段长途旅行或一条艰难的行动路线
senses.example: They undertook the crossing in small boats at night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夜里乘小船完成了这次横渡。
senses.why: A journey is taken up like a load: you commit your body to it before you know the end.
senses.whyCN: 旅程像货物一样被扛起：在知道结局之前，你就先把身体交付出去。

intro.en: Undertake is a native English compound of under and take, whose sense shifted from catching hold from below to taking a duty on oneself.
intro.cn: undertake 是英语本土复合词，由 under 与 take 组成，词义由「从下面接住」转为「把责任担到自己身上」。

items.en: Take comes from Old Norse taka, to grasp or seize, which replaced the Old English verb niman.
items.cn: take 来自古诺尔斯语 taka（抓取、拿），它取代了古英语动词 niman。

items.en: The compound first meant to intercept or catch hold of something, especially from below.
items.cn: 这个复合词最初意为拦截或接住某物，尤其指从下方托住。

items.en: From taking hold of a task came the sense of taking it upon oneself as a duty.
items.cn: 由「抓住一项任务」生出「把它作为职责担在自己身上」的意思。

items.en: The formal promise sense settled in, and undertake to do became common in contracts and letters.
items.cn: 正式的承诺义稳定下来，undertake to do 成为合同与书信中的常见说法。

items.en: Today the word covers research, repairs, journeys and any duty a person agrees to carry.
items.cn: 今天这个词涵盖研究、维修、旅程以及任何一个人同意承担的义务。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compounds in under- and the formally similar mistake word; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of assuming duties with different strength.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 under- 构成的复合词以及形似的易混词；近义组收表示承担职责的动词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: A person who arranges funerals; it is formed from undertake plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「殡葬承办人」，由 undertake 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A task or a formal promise; the noun form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「任务、承诺」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To pass another vehicle or to catch up with someone; the prefix is over, not under.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「超车、赶上」，前缀是 over 而不是 under。

entries.definition: The irregular past tense, used for a duty taken on in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则过去式，用于过去承担的职责。

entries.definition: An error, or to confuse one thing with another; it shares the take ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「错误」或动词「弄错」，只与 take 这一部分相同。

entries.definition: To take on a duty or role, often without being asked; more silent than undertake.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、就任」，常指未被要求便接下，比 undertake 更少声张。

entries.definition: The everyday phrasal verb for accepting work or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「承担、接受工作或责任」，最为口语。

entries.definition: To promise time, money, or effort to something; stresses locking oneself in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投入、承诺」，强调把自己锁定在某事上。

entries.definition: To begin something new and large, especially a project or journey.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「着手、开始」，多指宏大而新的事业或旅程。

entries.definition: A general verb for agreeing to receive or do something; it lacks the image of carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受」，属一般用语，不含「扛起」的意象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal pieces of the compound and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词的各个部件，以及这个词真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Under plus take: take the job up from underneath and hold it.
normal.cn: under 加 take：从下面把活儿托起来抓住。

normal.en: A team undertakes a survey; a builder undertakes the repairs.
normal.cn: 团队承担调查；建筑商承办维修。

normal.en: Undertake to do something is a formal promise, as in a contract.
normal.cn: undertake to do something 是正式承诺，常见于合同。

normal.en: The past form is undertook, the participle is undertaken.
normal.cn: 过去式是 undertook，过去分词是 undertaken。

normal.en: An undertaker takes on the last duty for a family.
normal.cn: undertaker 是替一个家庭承担最后那件事的人。

abstract.en: Picture a load that has no handles: to move it you must get underneath, and that is exactly what the word says.
abstract.cn: 想象一包没有提手的东西：要搬动它你必须钻到底下，而这正是这个词说的动作。

abstract.en: Every obligation is weight: undertake measures how much of it you agree to lift.
abstract.cn: 每项义务都有重量：undertake 衡量的是你同意抬起多少。

abstract.en: The word joins promise and effort, so saying it commits both the voice and the hands.
abstract.cn: 这个词把承诺与力气系在一起，说出口就等于同时交出了声音和双手。

examples.en: She undertook the difficult task of rebuilding the school library.
examples.cn: 她承担了重建学校图书馆这项艰难任务。

examples.en: The company has undertaken to reduce its waste by half.
examples.cn: 公司已承诺把废弃物减少一半。

examples.en: Two students undertook a study of traffic near the school gate.
examples.cn: 两名学生对学校门口的交通状况开展了研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的退克」——安退一步，把重活扛上肩：承担、承诺

root: 由 under（古英语 under，在下）与 take（古诺尔斯语 taka，抓取）合成；早期义为「从下面承接、拦截」，中古英语起转为「把任务担在自己身上」，近代定型为承担与正式承诺。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of undertake all describe one movement: getting beneath a weight and agreeing to carry it, whether it is work, a promise, a study, a contract, or a journey.
sensesIntro.cn: undertake 的五个义项都描述同一个动作：钻到重物下方并同意去扛它，无论那是工作、承诺、研究、合同还是旅程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone crouches, slides under a heavy load, and stands up carrying it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人蹲下，钻到重物底下，然后扛着它站起来。

branches.en: THE WORK: a task is accepted and carried from the first day.
branches.cn: 工作线：任务被接受，并从第一天起就扛着走。

branches.en: THE WORD GIVEN: the same load is promised out loud.
branches.cn: 言辞线：同一份重负被说出口地承诺下来。

branches.en: THE STUDY: research and surveys are long loads that must be lifted first.
branches.cn: 研究线：研究与调查是需要先抬起来的长途重负。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: in law the word records who has agreed to carry what.
branches.cn: 合同线：在法律上这个词记录谁同意扛什么。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY: a long road is taken up as a load is taken up.
branches.cn: 旅程线：漫长的路像重物一样被扛起。

intro.en: Undertake is built from a native prefix and a borrowed Norse verb, and the noun family grows with English suffixes.
intro.cn: undertake 由一个本土前缀与一个借自诺尔斯语的动词构成，名词家族由英语后缀生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Neither piece is Latin: under is native and taka is Old Norse, so the Latin table here records only later scholarly relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是拉丁语：under 是本土词，taka 是古诺尔斯语；此处的拉丁条目只记录后世的学术同源词。

items.example: The prefix shows the load being lifted from below.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示重物是从下面被抬起的。

items.example: The verb names the grip on the task.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指对任务的抓握。

items.example: Norse settlers brought the verb into English.
items.exampleCN: 诺尔斯移民把这个动词带入英语。

items.example: The older native verb was pushed out by taka.
items.exampleCN: 更早的本土动词被 taka 取代。

items.example: The irregular past keeps the old vowel pattern.
items.exampleCN: 不规则过去式保留了古老的元音变化。

items.meaning: one who takes on a task
items.example: Its modern sense shifted to funerals only.
items.exampleCN: 其现代义已缩窄到殡葬承办。

definition_zh: 水下的；在水中的；水下使用的
definition_en: lying, happening, or used below the surface of the sea, a lake, or a river
core_image: 一个人把头埋进清亮的水面以下，看见阳光在头顶碎成一片晃动的光斑
scene: 潜摄小组清晨出发，海面平静得像一块玻璃。An underwater camera filmed the coral reef for two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 underwater 是「水下的」（第 1 个义项：位于水面以下）；句意为一台水下摄像机把珊瑚礁拍了两小时。沉到水面以下的那个世界，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 水下；水中部分（少见用法）

derivatives.zh: 由同义近形词构成，义为「海底的」
由拉丁语 sub-「在下」加 mergere「浸入」构成，义为「被水淹没的」

senses.title: Below the surface
senses.definition: situated or happening below the surface of a body of water
senses.definitionCN: 位于或发生在水体表面以下
senses.example: The divers spent an hour underwater looking for the wreck.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在水下待了一小时寻找那艘沉船。
senses.why: Under is beneath and water is water: the word simply puts one thing below the other.
senses.whyCN: under 是「在下面」，water 是「水」：这个词就是把一样东西放到另一样下面。

senses.title: Made for use down there
senses.definition: designed, built, or used for working below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 为在水面以下工作而设计、建造或使用的
senses.example: The crew lowered an underwater light to film the fish at night.
senses.exampleCN: 船员放下了一盏水下灯，在夜里拍鱼。
senses.why: Anything that has to work down there must survive pressure and water, so the word marks equipment by its place.
senses.whyCN: 凡要在那里工作的东西都得扛住水压与水，于是这个词以地点来标记器材。

senses.title: Swimming below the surface
senses.definition: moving, swimming, or staying beneath the surface rather than on it
senses.definitionCN: 在水面以下而非水面之上移动、游泳或停留
senses.example: Sea otters can swim underwater for several minutes at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 海獭一次能在水下游泳好几分钟。
senses.why: Used after a verb, the same word tells where the action happens.
senses.whyCN: 放在动词之后，同一个词说明动作发生在哪里。

senses.title: The submerged part
senses.definition: the part of a rock, hull, or structure that lies beneath the waterline
senses.definitionCN: 岩石、船体或建筑物位于水线以下的部分
senses.example: Engineers inspected the underwater of the pier for cracks.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查了桥墩水下部分是否有裂缝。
senses.why: The word can be turned into a noun for the hidden half of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以名词化，指一样东西藏在水下的那一半。

senses.title: In debt: sunk below
senses.titleCN: 资不抵债：沉到水面以下
senses.definition: in the phrase underwater on a loan, owing more than the property is worth
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 underwater on a loan，指欠款超过抵押物价值
senses.example: After the flood the family was underwater on its mortgage.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后，这家的房贷已经资不抵债。
senses.why: Financially the image is exact: the borrower is below the line, and the water over his head is debt.
senses.whyCN: 在财务上这个比喻很贴切：借款人沉在水线以下，头顶的水就是债。

intro.en: Underwater is a transparent English compound of two native roots, first used when people began to write about diving and the sea floor.
intro.cn: underwater 是结构透明的英语复合词，两个部件都是本土词根，人们开始描写潜水与海底时才用起来。

items.en: Under is Old English under, beneath, and wæter is the native word for water.
items.cn: under 是古英语 under（在下面），wæter 是表示水的本土词。

items.en: Both words descend from Germanic forms, and they have stood side by side since the earliest English.
items.cn: 两个词都源自日耳曼语形式，自最早的英语起就并立使用。

items.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries divers wrote of underwater work on wrecks and harbours.
items.cn: 十七与十八世纪，潜水员记录关于沉船与港口的水下作业时用了这个说法。

items.en: The nineteenth century added underwater cables, tunnels and photography.
items.cn: 十九世纪又添了水下电缆、隧道与水下摄影。

items.en: The word was later borrowed by finance for debt below the value line.
items.cn: 后来金融界借用了这个词，指价值线以下的债务。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compounds with under-; the near-meaning group gathers words for things below the surface with different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 under- 构成的复合词；近义组收表示水面以下事物的词，范围各有不同。

entries.definition: Below the surface of the ground, or the railway that runs there.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「地下的」，也指地下铁路。

entries.definition: Below the surface of the sea; close to underwater but usually about the sea only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「海底的」，与 underwater 接近，但通常只用于海。

entries.definition: Not letting water through; describes a material rather than a place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「防水的」，描述材料而非位置。

entries.definition: Already started and in progress; the second half is way, not water.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已开始的、进行中的」，后半部分是 way 而不是 water。

entries.definition: Further along a river in the direction the water flows.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「下游的」，指沿水流方向更远处。

entries.definition: Completely covered by water; stresses the fact of being drowned rather than the place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被淹没的」，强调被水盖住的状况而非位置。

entries.definition: A vessel that travels below the surface; also an adjective for undersea things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「潜艇」，也作形容词表示「海底的」。

entries.definition: Lying at the bottom, especially of a ship or a garden area set lower down.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「沉没的、下凹的」，多指沉船或下沉的庭院。

entries.definition: Of the open ocean far from land and far below the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深海的」，指远离陆地、水面很深的开放海域。

entries.definition: A formal adjective for life or activity below water; rare in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「水下的、水生的」，较正式，日常少见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two plain English pieces and the real phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的两个朴素英语部件，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Under plus water: wherever the word goes, it names a place below the surface.
normal.cn: under 加 water：这个词无论怎么用，指的都是水面以下的位置。

normal.en: An underwater camera must survive pressure, so it is named by where it works.
normal.cn: 水下摄像机必须扛住水压，因此以工作地点命名。

normal.en: Swim underwater uses the word as an adverb after the verb.
normal.cn: swim underwater 把这个词当副词放在动词之后。

normal.en: Separate the two words and under water means flooded, not undersea.
normal.cn: 分开写 under water 表示被水淹了，而不是在海底。

normal.en: Being underwater on a mortgage means owing more than the house is worth.
normal.cn: underwater on a mortgage 指欠的钱比房子价值还多。

abstract.en: Picture the waterline as a strict border: everything under it lives by different rules of light, sound and weight.
abstract.cn: 把水线想象成一条严格的边界：线以下的一切按另一套光、声与重量的规则生活。

abstract.en: The same word covers a camera, a reef and a debt, because all three have sunk below a line other people set.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指相机、礁石也指债务，因为三者都沉到了别人划出的某条线以下。

abstract.en: Underwater is not simply wet: it is a whole layer of the world with its own name.
abstract.cn: underwater 不只是「湿」：它是世界的一整个层次，有自己的名字。

examples.en: The underwater cave is home to blind fish and pale shrimp.
examples.cn: 这个水下洞穴里住着盲鱼和苍白的虾。

examples.en: He can hold his breath underwater for nearly two minutes.
examples.cn: 他在水下能憋气将近两分钟。

examples.en: Repair crews sent an underwater robot to check the broken pipe.
examples.cn: 维修队派出水下机器人检查破裂的管道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的渥特」——安潜到渥特河的水面以下：水下的

root: 由古英语 under（在下面）与 wæter（水）两个日耳曼语系本土词构成，字面就是「在水之下」；近代随潜水、海底工程与水下摄影而广泛使用，后来又借到金融里指资不抵债。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of underwater all keep one relation: something lies below the surface of water, whether it is a place, a tool, a movement, a hidden part, or a debt.
sensesIntro.cn: underwater 的五个义项都维持同一种关系：某物位于水面以下，无论那是地点、器材、动作、隐藏的部分还是债务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diver sinks through the bright surface into a green, quiet world below.
core.cn: 核心意象：潜水者穿过明亮的水面，沉入下方青绿而安静的世界。

branches.en: THE PLACE: whatever is under the surface is described by one word.
branches.cn: 地点线：凡是水面以下的事物都用这一个词描述。

branches.en: THE GEAR: cameras, lights and robots are named by where they must work.
branches.cn: 器材线：相机、灯与机器人都以必须工作的地方命名。

branches.en: THE MOTION: swimming beneath the surface uses the word as an adverb.
branches.cn: 动作线：在水面以下游泳时，这个词作副词用。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN HALF: a hull or a pier has an underwater part no one sees.
branches.cn: 隐藏线：船体或桥墩都有没人看得见的水下部分。

branches.en: THE DEBT: finance borrows the image for owing more than the value line.
branches.cn: 债务线：金融借用这个意象，指欠款超过价值线。

intro.en: Both halves of underwater are native English words, so the word has no Latin core at all.
intro.cn: underwater 的两半都是英语本土词，因此这个词完全没有拉丁词根核心。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here; the table below lists only the later Latin-based synonyms that name the same place.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；下表只列出后世以拉丁语为源、指同一位置的近义词。

items.example: The prefix fixes the position below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀锁定水面以下的位置。

items.meaning: the liquid of seas and rivers
items.example: The noun names the medium that covers the thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指覆盖该物的介质。

items.example: It appears in submerged and submarine.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 submerged 与 submarine 中。

items.example: It stresses being drowned rather than being below.
items.exampleCN: 它强调被水盖住而非位置在下面。

items.example: It uses sub plus marinus, of the sea.
items.exampleCN: 它由 sub 加表示「海的」marinus 构成。
underwater 的一个范围更窄的近亲。

items.example: The word is fully native in both halves.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的两半都是完全的英语本土成分。

items.meaning: the line where water touches a hull
items.example: The border that underwater refers to.
items.exampleCN: 正是 underwater 所指的那条界线。

definition_zh: 失业；失业状态；失业人数；失业率
definition_en: the state of having no job and looking for work, or the number of people in that state
core_image: 工厂大门紧闭，一群人抱着简历站在门外，门上的招聘牌被撤了下来
scene: 冬天下着小雪，镇上的纺织厂在清晨贴出停产通知，工人们围在门口不肯散去。Unemployment in the town doubled within a single winter.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployment 是「失业、失业状况」（第 1 个义项：没有工作并正在找工作）；句意为这个镇的失业人数在一个冬天里翻了一倍。关着的厂门与门外的人，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 un- 加 employed 构成，义为「失业的；未被利用的」
由拉丁语 implicare 经法语构成，义为「雇用；使用」
由 employ 加 -ment 构成，义为「就业；雇用」
由 employ 加 -er 构成，义为「雇主」

senses.title: The state of having no work
senses.definition: the situation of being without a paid job while wanting and looking for one
senses.definitionCN: 没有有偿工作而仍希望并寻找工作的处境
senses.example: Unemployment among young graduates rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年年轻的大学毕业生失业率急剧上升。
senses.why: Un- strips away the thing that employ gives, and -ment names the state that is left.
senses.whyCN: un- 把 employ 所给的东西拿掉，-ment 命名剩下的那个状态。

senses.title: The jobless counted together
senses.definition: the number or proportion of people in a country or area who have no work
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区中没有工作的人数或比例
senses.example: The government reported that unemployment had reached nine percent.
senses.exampleCN: 政府报告称失业率已达到百分之九。
senses.why: Statistics turned the personal situation into a public figure that can be measured month by month.
senses.whyCN: 统计数据把个人处境变成了可逐月衡量的公共数字。

senses.title: Money for those without work
senses.definition: in British English, money paid by the state to people who have no job
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中，国家付给没有工作的人的钱
senses.example: He was on unemployment for six months before finding factory work.
senses.exampleCN: 在找到工厂的工作之前，他领了六个月的失业救济。
senses.why: The abstract state became a concrete payment, as names for hard conditions often do.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的状态变成了具体的给付，描述艰难处境的名称常常这样转义。

senses.title: A machine or field out of production
senses.definition: of land, machinery, or capital: lying unused while it could be productive
senses.definitionCN: 土地、机器或资本本可发挥作用却处于闲置状态
senses.example: Economists noted the unemployment of the mills and the warehouses beside them.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家指出了那些闲置的磨坊以及旁边的仓库。
senses.why: The word can be taken literally: any resource that no one has put to work is unemployed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可按字面理解：任何没有被投入使用的资源都是「失业」的。

senses.title: A social problem by a name
senses.titleCN: 一个作为社会问题的名称
senses.definition: used as a heading for the social and political problem caused by mass joblessness
senses.definitionCN: 用作一个标题式说法，指大规模无工作所造成的社会与政治问题
senses.example: The report treated unemployment as the town's deepest and most difficult problem.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把失业视为这个镇最深、最难解决的问题。
senses.why: A word about individuals became a topic for policy: the same state, seen from above.
senses.whyCN: 一个关于个人的词变成了政策议题：同一个状态，换到高处去看。

intro.en: Unemployment is a modern English construction: a negative prefix and a set of English and French suffixes around a Latin verb.
intro.cn: unemployment 是近代英语的构造：否定前缀与一串英语、法语后缀围绕一个拉丁语动词。

items.en: Implicare meant to enfold or involve; the French verb employer took on the sense of using or engaging.
items.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「包裹、卷入」；法语动词 employer 生出「使用、雇用」义。

items.en: English borrowed the French verb as employ, to use or to give work to.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语动词作 employ，表示使用或给予工作。

items.en: The noun employer and the derived noun employment passed into English in the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 名词 employer 与派生名词 employment 在中世纪末期进入英语。

items.en: In the nineteenth century employers and unions began to speak of unemployment as a condition of whole industries.
items.cn: 十九世纪，雇主与工会开始把失业当作整个行业的一种状况来谈论。

items.en: Measurement turned it into a statistic, and the rate of unemployment became a standard figure of public debate.
items.cn: 统计测量把它变成一项数据，失业率成为公共讨论中的标准数字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same employ root; the near-meaning group gathers words for idleness or jobless conditions that differ in scope.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 employ 词根上的词；近义组收表示闲置或无业状况的词，范围不同。

entries.definition: The adjective for a person or resource with no work; the noun form is the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失业的」，名词形式则指这种状态本身。

entries.definition: The noun for paid work itself, the opposite of unemployment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就业、雇用」，是 unemployment 的反面。

entries.definition: A person who is hired and paid to work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇员」。

entries.definition: A person or company that hires others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇主」。

entries.definition: The act of moving troops or resources into position; close in spelling, different in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部署」，拼写相近而意义不同。

entries.definition: The plain noun for having no job; less tied to official statistics than unemployment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无业」，比 unemployment 更少与官方统计挂钩。

entries.definition: Job loss because a post is no longer needed; a British term, often with compensation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「裁员、冗员」，英式用法，常涉及补偿。

entries.definition: The state of not working or being unused; it can describe people or machines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「懒散、闲置」，可用于人或机器。

entries.definition: A temporary or permanent dismissal of workers for economic reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「裁员、停工解雇」，因经济原因暂时或永久辞退工人。

entries.definition: The state of working fewer hours or below one's skill level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不充分就业」，工时不足或低于自身技能水平。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the negative prefix, the root meaning to use, and the public figures the word belongs to.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用否定前缀、表示「使用」的词根，以及这个词所归属的公共数据。

normal.en: Un- means not, employ means put to use, -ment means state: not being put to work.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，employ 表示「使用」，-ment 表示「状态」：不被投入使用。

normal.en: The unemployment rate is the headline figure in every budget speech.
normal.cn: 失业率是每场预算演说里的头号数据。

normal.en: In British English, to be on unemployment is to receive the jobless benefit.
normal.cn: 在英式英语里，be on unemployment 就是领取失业救济。

normal.en: Employer and employee sit on the two sides of employment.
normal.cn: 雇主与雇员站在就业的两边。

normal.en: Idle mills, empty warehouses: resources too can be unemployed.
normal.cn: 停摆的磨坊、空着的仓库：资源也会失业。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with a job notice taken down: the people outside have not changed, only the work has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被摘下招工牌子：门外的人没有变，消失的是工作。

abstract.en: One word holds a personal winter and a national figure, because it can be counted.
abstract.cn: 一个词里同时装进一个人的冬天和一个国家的数字，因为它能被统计。

abstract.en: Unemployment names an absence, and absences are hardest to see until someone counts them.
abstract.cn: unemployment 命名的是缺失，而缺失在有人去数之前最难被看见。

examples.en: Unemployment fell for the third month in a row.
examples.cn: 失业率连续第三个月下降。

examples.en: The plant closure brought unemployment to a village that had always had work.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭使这个一向有活儿干的村子陷入失业。

examples.en: She is studying the unemployment of rural women in three provinces.
examples.cn: 她正在研究三个省份农村女性的失业问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安普洛依门特」——安没被雇主收进门：失业

root: 由 un-「不」加 employment（就业）构成；employment 源自法语 employer，再上溯拉丁语 implicare「包裹、卷入」，近代英语把「不就业的状态」独立成词，并由此生出失业人数、失业率与失业救济等用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unemployment all name one absence, the lack of paid work, seen as a person's state, a statistic, a payment, an idle resource, or a public problem.
sensesIntro.cn: unemployment 的五个义项都在命名同一种缺失，即有偿工作的缺席，只是分别看作个人状态、统计数据、给付、闲置资源与公共问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the factory gate is shut and the job notice has been taken down.
core.cn: 核心意象：工厂大门紧闭，招工启事已经被撤下。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a woman or man without paid work, still looking.
branches.cn: 个人线：没有有偿工作、仍在寻找机会的人。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: the same state counted across a region and published monthly.
branches.cn: 数字线：同一状态在地区范围内被计数并按月公布。

branches.en: THE PAYMENT: the state turns into money from the state.
branches.cn: 给付线：这种状态转成了国家给出的钱。

branches.en: THE RESOURCE: machines and land can be unemployed too.
branches.cn: 资源线：机器与土地也会处于闲置状态。

branches.en: THE AGENDA: mass joblessness becomes a topic of policy and debate.
branches.cn: 议题线：大规模无工作成为政策与争论的话题。

intro.en: Unemployment stacks a negative prefix, a Latin-derived root, and two noun suffixes, which is why it looks long.
intro.cn: unemployment 层叠了否定前缀、拉丁语来源的词根与两个名词后缀，所以看上去很长。

latinIntro.en: Latin implicare is recorded, and French employer stands between it and the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 有文献记录，法语 employer 位于它与英语词之间。

items.example: The prefix denies that work is present.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否认工作的存在。

items.example: It marks being folded into a job or use.
items.exampleCN: 它表示被卷进一项工作或用途中。

items.example: The old root lies inside employ.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老词根藏在 employ 里面。

items.example: It appears in deployment, a look-alike word.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在形近词 deployment 中。

items.example: The Latin verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族背后的拉丁动词。

latinEntries.structure: Old French verb from Latin implicare

definition_zh: 制服；校服；军服；统一的；一律的；一致的
definition_en: the special clothes worn by members of a school, service, or team, or being the same in every part
core_image: 一排学生穿着同一款式同一颜色同一尺码的校服，站成一条整齐的直线
scene: 开学第一天，校门口有位女老师拿着尺子检查每个人的衣领和袖口。Every student wore the same blue uniform, down to the buttons.
sceneCN: 这里 uniform 是「校服、制服」（第 1 个义项：同一团体成员穿的同款服装）；句意为每个学生都穿着同样的蓝色校服，连纽扣都一样。排成一排的同款衣服，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 均匀的；无变化的（速度、质地）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「一致地；均匀地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「一致性；一律」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「穿制服的」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「没有制服的」

senses.title: Clothes that mark a group
senses.definition: a set of clothes that all members of a school, service, or team wear
senses.definitionCN: 某学校、部队或团队的成员全部穿着的成套服装
senses.example: Nurses at the city hospital wear a white uniform.
senses.exampleCN: 市医院的护士穿白色制服。
senses.why: Uni- is one and form is shape: one shape of dress for many bodies.
senses.whyCN: uni- 是「一」，form 是「形状」：许多身体只穿一种形状的衣服。

senses.title: The same in every part
senses.definition: being the same in size, style, or rules everywhere, without variation
senses.definitionCN: 在尺寸、样式或规则上处处相同，没有变化
senses.example: All branches follow a uniform set of safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有分店都遵循一套统一的安全规则。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the very image of the clothes: one form applied everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留的正是衣服的意象：一种形式被用到处处。

senses.title: Steady and even
senses.definition: remaining at a constant level or rate, without speeding up or slowing down
senses.definitionCN: 保持在恒定水平或速率上，不快也不慢
senses.example: A falling object moves in nearly uniform acceleration near the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 落体在地面附近几乎做匀加速运动。
senses.why: In physics one form must also mean one rate: nothing in the motion changes shape.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学里，一种形式也要求一种速率：运动中没有任何部分改变样子。

senses.title: To make things alike
senses.definition: to bring parts or rules into one form, so that all are alike
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分或规则归成一种形式，使它们彼此相同
senses.example: The new manager uniformed the labels across the whole warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 新任经理把整个仓库的标签统一了起来。
senses.why: The verb turns the state into an action: someone decides what the one form shall be.
senses.whyCN: 动词把状态变成动作：由某个人来决定那唯一的形式是什么。

senses.title: Members of the service
senses.definition: used with the to mean the police, soldiers, or other people in uniform
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指警察、士兵或其他穿制服的人
senses.example: The crowd stepped aside quickly when the uniform arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 穿制服的人一到，人群立刻让开。
senses.why: By a familiar shift, the clothing stands for whoever wears it.
senses.whyCN: 衣服代替了穿它的人，这是常见的转义。

intro.en: Uniform joins a Latin word for one to a Latin word for shape, and the pair entered English through French.
intro.cn: uniform 把拉丁语表示「一」的词与表示「形状」的词拼在一起，再经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one, and forma meant a shape, mould, or appearance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，forma 意为「形状、模子、外观」。

items.en: Uniformis was used for what keeps a single form, and the schools applied it to evenness of quality.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 uniformis 指保持单一形式的事物，经院学者用它表示质性齐一。

items.en: French uniforme carried both the abstract sense of even and same and, later, the sense of a dress.
items.cn: 法语 uniforme 既有「一律、相同」的抽象义，后来又生出了服装义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century soldiers and servants were dressed alike, and uniform came to mean the dress itself.
items.cn: 十七世纪起士兵与仆役制服整齐，uniform 由此转指这套衣服。

items.en: Schools, hospitals and transport staff adopted uniforms, while science kept the sense of uniform speed and uniform law.
items.cn: 学校、医院与交通部门采用制服，科学界则保留匀速与统一规律的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on uni- and forma; the near-meaning group gathers words for clothing and for sameness with different emphasis.
note.cn: 形近组收以 uni- 与 forma 构成的词；近义组收表示服装与一致性的词，侧重点不同。

entries.definition: The noun for being the same everywhere; the quality behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一致性、一律」，是形容词背后的性质。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in the same way everywhere, or at an even rate.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「一致地、均匀地」。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who is wearing a uniform.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「穿制服的」。

entries.definition: To make separate parts into one whole; it shares the one part but not the shape.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「统一、使成一体」，共享「一」这一部分而非形状。

entries.definition: A shape or a printed paper; the second half of uniform on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形状、表格」，即 uniform 的后半部分。

entries.definition: Always the same in behaviour or standard; usually about actions rather than looks.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一贯的、一致的」，多指行为或标准而非外观。

entries.definition: An agreed level or pattern that things should meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「标准」，指应达到的既定水平或样式。

entries.definition: A set of clothes worn together, with no idea of group membership.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一套衣服」，不含团体属含义。

entries.definition: The distinctive dress given to servants or staff of a household.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「号衣、仆役制服」，历史上大户人家发给仆人的服装。

entries.definition: An official rule, or the plain clothing required by one, as in regulation dress.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规定」，也可指规定所要求的朴素服装。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin pieces, one and form, and the ordinary phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个拉丁部件「一」与「形」，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- means one and form means shape: one shape of clothing for everyone.
normal.cn: uni- 表示「一」，form 表示「形状」：所有人只穿一种形状的衣服。

normal.en: School uniform, military uniform, in uniform: the phrase always marks belonging.
normal.cn: school uniform、military uniform、in uniform：这些搭配都在标记归属。

normal.en: Uniform rules and uniform speed keep one form across space and time.
normal.cn: 统一规则与匀速运动都在空间与时间上保持同一形式。

normal.en: Uniform is also a physics word, as in uniform motion.
normal.cn: uniform 也是物理术语，如匀速运动 uniform motion。

normal.en: The uniform can stand for the person: the crowd quietened when the uniform came.
normal.cn: 制服可以代替人：制服一到，人群就安静了。

abstract.en: Picture many shoulders under cloth cut once: the individual is still there, but the outline is shared.
abstract.cn: 想象许多肩膀罩在同一块剪裁好的布下：个人还在，轮廓却是共享的。

abstract.en: A uniform is a promise made visible: whoever wears it agrees to be seen as one of a group.
abstract.cn: 制服是看得见的承诺：谁穿上它，就同意被看作团体中的一员。

abstract.en: From clothes to rules to speed, the word always asks whether everything really has the same shape.
abstract.cn: 从服装到规则再到速度，这个词始终在问：所有东西真的都是同一个形状吗。

examples.en: He keeps his old army uniform folded in a wooden box.
examples.cn: 他把旧军装叠好放在一只木箱里。

examples.en: The two schools agreed on a uniform exam paper.
examples.cn: 两所学校商定使用统一的试卷。

examples.en: The train moved at a uniform speed along the straight track.
examples.cn: 列车沿笔直的轨道匀速前进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼佛姆」——优尼一人一件佛姆款：统一的制服

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 forma「形状」，中世纪拉丁语 uniformis 指「保持单一形式、性质齐一」，经法语 uniforme 进入英语，十七世纪起转指统一的服装，科学中也保留「匀速、统一规律」的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of uniform all hold one idea: a single shape imposed on many things, whether clothes, rules, speed, labels, or the people who wear them.
sensesIntro.cn: uniform 的五个义项都守住同一个观念：把单一的形状施加到许多对象上，无论那是衣服、规则、速度、标签，还是穿它的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of students in identical blue clothes with identical buttons.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排学生穿着同样的蓝色衣服，纽扣也一模一样。

branches.en: THE CLOTHES: one cut of cloth worn by a whole group.
branches.cn: 服装线：一整个团体都穿同一种剪裁的布。

branches.en: THE RULES: the same standard applied everywhere without exception.
branches.cn: 规则线：同一标准被无例外地用到处处。

branches.en: THE RATE: in physics the form and the speed must stay one.
branches.cn: 速率线：在物理中形式与速度都必须保持同一。

branches.en: THE ACT: someone brings parts into the one form.
branches.cn: 动作线：由某人把各部分归入那唯一的形式。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: the clothing stands for the person who wears it.
branches.cn: 人物线：衣服代替了穿衣服的人。

intro.en: Uniform is a Latin prefix-root pair with an English suffix family grown on top.
intro.cn: uniform 是一对拉丁语前缀与词根，上面又长出一族英语后缀词。

latinIntro.en: Both unus and forma are recorded Latin words, and uniformis is recorded in medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus 与 forma 都有文献记录，uniformis 见于中世纪拉丁语。

items.example: The prefix supplies the idea of oneness.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供「唯一」的意思。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「形状」的意思。

items.example: The Latin source of the second half.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The recorded Latin form of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 整词在中世纪拉丁语中的形式。

items.example: A cousin built on the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: 用同一前缀构成的近亲词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 具有一种形式的；一律的

definition_zh: 独一无二的；唯一的；独特的；极好的；罕见的
definition_en: being the only one of its kind, or unusually special and good
core_image: 一整块原石被凿成一只瓶，世上再没有第二只，连模具也没有留下来
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里放着一只烧坏的窑变瓷瓶，釉色在灯下像流动的水。The curator says this unique piece cannot be copied, even by the same kiln.
sceneCN: 这里 unique 是「独一无二的」（第 1 个义项：同类中仅此一件）；句意为馆长说这件孤品即使同一座窑也复制不出来。柜中那只没有第二件的瓷瓶，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「独特地；唯一地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「独特性；唯一性」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「唯一性」（较少用）

senses.title: The only one of its kind
senses.definition: existing as the single example of its kind, so that nothing else is the same
senses.definitionCN: 作为同类中的唯一存在，没有别的东西与它相同
senses.example: Each fingerprint is unique, even between identical twins.
senses.exampleCN: 每个指纹都是独一无二的，即使同卵双胞胎之间也不同。
senses.why: Latin unus means one: the word points to a class with only one member.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」：这个词所指的那一类里只有一名成员。

senses.title: Belonging to one thing only
senses.definition: belonging to or found in only one place, person, or group
senses.definitionCN: 只属于或只出现在某一个地方、人或群体
senses.example: This dialect is unique to a few fishing villages on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言只存在于沿海几个渔村。
senses.why: Uniqueness can be claimed for a thing by pointing at the one place it occurs.
senses.whyCN: 只要指出它唯一出现的地方，就能为某物主张独有性。

senses.title: Unusually special
senses.definition: unusually good, special, or rare, so as to seem unlike anything else
senses.definitionCN: 格外好、特别或罕见，以至于显得不同寻常
senses.example: She has a unique gift for making shy children speak.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种难得的天赋，能让害羞的孩子开口说话。
senses.why: Marketers and speakers stretch the word from only one to one of a kind in quality.
senses.whyCN: 广告与演讲把这个词从「只有一个」扩展到「品质上独一类」。

senses.title: The one thing itself
senses.definition: a rare noun use for the single object or person that has no match
senses.definitionCN: 少见的名词用法，指没有相配之物的那一个对象或人
senses.example: Collectors speak of the unique, the piece that no museum can pair.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏家会说起「孤品」，那种任何博物馆都配不成对的物件。
senses.why: Adjectives for state are often turned into nouns, and this one names the matchless thing.
senses.whyCN: 表示状态的形容词常转作名词，这个词指那件无从配对之物。

senses.title: As a key in systems
senses.definition: in computing, identifying one record or account and no other
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指只标识一条记录或一个账户而不标识其他
senses.example: Every account is given a unique number that is never reused.
senses.exampleCN: 每个账户都被分配一个从不重复使用的唯一编号。
senses.why: Machines need the strict sense: one identifier, one record, no exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 机器需要最严格的意义：一个标识对应一条记录，没有例外。

intro.en: Unique comes from a Latin word built on one, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: unique 来自一个以「一」为核心构成的拉丁语词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one, and the adjective unicus meant single, sole, of one only.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，形容词 unicus 意为「唯一的、单独的」。

items.en: French took unicus as un, and formed univ meaning only one, the source of the English word.
items.cn: 法语把 unicus 化约成 un，并构成 univ，义为「只有一个」，是英语词的来源。

items.en: Sixteenth-century French unique was used for the sole example of a thing, with no rival.
items.cn: 十六世纪的法语 unique 用于指某物唯一的实例，没有对手。

items.en: English borrowed the word for things that stand alone in their class, from coins to paintings.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，指在其类别中单独存在的对象，从钱币到绘画。

items.en: The weaker sense of merely unusual or very good spread in advertising and everyday praise.
items.cn: 「仅仅罕见或很好」这种较弱的意义在广告与日常赞美中扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the one root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of rarity and distinction at different strengths.
note.cn: 形近组收以「一」这一词根构成的词；近义组收表示稀有与出众的形容词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that belongs to no other.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「独特地、唯一地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being the only one of its kind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「独特性、唯一性」。

entries.definition: Speaking or singing at the same pitch together; it shares the one but not the sole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「齐声、同音」，共享「一」而不含「唯一」。

entries.definition: A single thing or measure treated as one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「单位、单元」，即被当作一个的整体。

entries.definition: The joining of separate things into one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联合、工会」，把分开之物合成一个。

entries.definition: Exceptional or odd; in grammar, one rather than many.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非凡的、奇特的」，语法中表示单数。

entries.definition: The only one there is, as in the sole owner; narrower and more legal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「唯一的」，如唯一所有人，范围更窄、更偏法律。

entries.definition: Not often found; it does not claim that only one exists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稀少的」，并不主张只有一件。

entries.definition: Easy to tell apart from others; about difference rather than number.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有特色的」，强调区别而非数量。

entries.definition: Having no equal at all; a stronger, more formal claim than unique.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无与伦比的」，比 unique 更强、更正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin one at the centre of the word and the phrases it really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词核心处的拉丁语「一」，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one: a unique thing is a class with a single member.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」：unique 之物就是只有一个成员的那一类。

normal.en: Fingerprints are the textbook example: unique even for twins.
normal.cn: 指纹是教科书式的例子：连双胞胎之间也独一无二。

normal.en: Unique to means found in one place only.
normal.cn: unique to 意为只存在于某一处。

normal.en: The word has no true comparative in strict use: something cannot be more one of a kind.
normal.cn: 严格来说这个词没有真正的比较级：一样东西不能更「独一份」。

normal.en: In computing a unique number may never be reused.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，唯一编号绝不可以重复使用。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut for one lock only: no copy of the blank exists, so the key is its own justification.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只为一把锁配出的钥匙：坯子没有第二份，钥匙本身就说明了一切。

abstract.en: Uniqueness is a relation, not a quality: a thing is unique only when compared with the whole class.
abstract.cn: 独特性是一种关系而非性质：只有与整个类别相比，一样东西才成立为唯一。

abstract.en: Advertising loves the word because it turns rarity into worth.
abstract.cn: 广告喜欢这个词，因为它把稀有变成了价值。

examples.en: This valley has a unique climate, with rain on one side and dry wind on the other.
examples.cn: 这条山谷的气候独一无二，一侧多雨，另一侧却是干风。

examples.en: The custom is unique to the islanders.
examples.cn: 这一习俗为岛上居民所特有。

examples.en: Each ticket carries a unique code for entry.
examples.cn: 每张票都带有一个入场专用的唯一编码。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼克」——优尼这一款只有一件，克数也不重样：独一无二

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」所生的 unicus「唯一的、单独的」，经古法语与法语 univ 进入英语；本义是「同类中仅此一件」，近代又扩展出「罕见、极好」的较弱意义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unique all turn on the number one: one member of a class, one place of origin, one of a kind in quality, the matchless object itself, or one key in a system.
sensesIntro.cn: unique 的五个义项都围绕「一」：类别里只有一员、只出现在一处、品质上独一类、那件无从配对之物本身，或系统中唯一的一把钥匙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single vessel fired once, with no mould left and no second copy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只只烧过一次的瓷器，模具没有留下，也没有第二件。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the word marks a class with only one member.
branches.cn: 类别线：这个词标记一个只有一名成员的类别。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the one location or group that has it.
branches.cn: 地点线：拥有它的那唯一一处地方或人群。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: rarity turns into praise of quality.
branches.cn: 赞美线：稀有转为对品质的赞美。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the matchless thing can be named as a noun.
branches.cn: 物件线：那件无从配对之物可用名词来命名。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: machines need one number for one record.
branches.cn: 系统线：机器需要一号对一记录。

intro.en: Unique is almost all root: a Latin word for one, plus a small adjective ending and English suffixes.
intro.cn: unique 几乎全是词根：一个拉丁语「一」词，加一个小小的形容词词尾与英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unicus are both recorded Latin words, so nothing in the core is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus 与 unicus 均有文献记录，核心部分不需要重构。

items.example: The prefix is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀是这个词的核心。

items.example: Latin unicus carried this ending into French.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 unicus 带着这个词尾进入法语。

items.example: A French cousin on the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根上的法语近亲。

items.example: An English word built on the same one.
items.exampleCN: 以同一个「一」构成的英语词。

definition_zh: 普遍的；全体的；通用的；宇宙的
definition_en: true of or shared by everyone or everything, or able to be used in all cases
core_image: 一张巨大的圆顶把天南地北的人与物全罩在里面，没有一处露在边缘之外
scene: 孩子们在课堂上争论笑容是不是人人都懂，老师让全班用自己的语言演示同一个表情。Smiling appears to be universal across every culture.
sceneCN: 这里 universal 是「普遍的、人人都有的」（第 1 个义项：对所有人都成立）；句意为微笑似乎在所有文化中都是普遍的。罩住一切的那个圆顶，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 普遍的；全体的；人人都有的
普遍概念；通用规律（哲学用法）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；人人皆然地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「普遍性；通用性」
与本词同源，义为「宇宙；全体」
与本词同源，义为「大学」，原指师生的全体团体

senses.title: True of everyone
senses.definition: applying to or shared by all people or all things of a kind
senses.definitionCN: 适用于某类的所有人或所有事物，或为其所共有
senses.example: The desire for safety is universal among parents.
senses.exampleCN: 对安全的渴望在父母心中是普遍的。
senses.why: Unus is one and versus is turned towards one: the whole field is gathered into a single reach.
senses.whyCN: unus 是「一」，versus 是「朝向一个」：整片领域被收进同一个范围。

senses.title: Usable in all cases
senses.definition: designed to work or apply in every case, without special adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 无需特别调整即可在任何情形下使用或适用
senses.example: A universal charger saves travellers from carrying five cables.
senses.exampleCN: 一只通用充电器让旅客不必带五根线。
senses.why: The adjective extends from people to tools: one form that fits everything.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从人扩展到工具：一种形式适合一切。

senses.title: Of the whole universe
senses.definition: relating to the whole of space and everything in it
senses.definitionCN: 与整个空间及其中的一切有关的
senses.example: Gravity is a universal force, acting on every mass in space.
senses.exampleCN: 引力是一种宇宙之力，作用于太空中的每个质量。
senses.why: In philosophy the word already meant the whole of things, and astronomy borrowed that reach.
senses.whyCN: 在哲学中这个词本已指万物的全体，天文学借用了这份范围。

senses.title: A general concept
senses.definition: in philosophy, a quality or concept said of many things rather than of one
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指可被多个事物共有的性质或概念，而非单个事物
senses.example: Medieval thinkers argued about whether universals exist apart from things.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪思想家争论普遍概念是否存在于事物之外。
senses.why: Logic needs a name for what many share, and the word for whole becomes that name.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要为众多事物共有之物命名，表示「全体」的词就成了这个名字。

senses.title: Everyone, without exception
senses.titleCN: 全体一致的；无一例外的
senses.definition: in phrases such as universal approval, agreeing by all without a single objection
senses.definitionCN: 在 universal approval 等说法中，指全体同意、没有一票反对
senses.example: The new playground won universal approval at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 新游乐场在会上获得一致赞同。
senses.why: Here the word does not describe a law but counts people: nobody is left outside.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不描述规律而在数人：没有一个人被留在外面。

intro.en: Universal is built on the same Latin pair as universe: one, and turning towards one whole.
intro.cn: universal 与 universe 建立在同一对拉丁语词上：「一」，以及「转向同一整体」。

items.en: Unus meant one, and the verb vertere meant to turn; the pair gave universus, turned into one, whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，动词 vertere 意为「转动」；二者合出 universus，即「合成一个、整个的」。

items.en: Late Latin universalis meant belonging to all, and it was the adjective used in logic and law.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 universalis 意为「属于全体的」，是逻辑学与法学里的形容词。

items.en: French universal carried the sense of general and applied to all cases.
items.cn: 法语 universal 带有「一般的、适用于一切情形」的意思。

items.en: Scholastic writers used universal for concepts shared by many things.
items.cn: 经院作者用 universal 指众多事物共有的概念。

items.en: Natural science took up the word for laws holding everywhere, and everyday speech took it for what everyone shares.
items.cn: 自然科学取它表示处处成立的定律，日常言语则取它表示人人共有之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same one-and-turn root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of scope with different breadth.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「合一」词根上的词；近义组收表示范围的形容词，宽窄不同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning by everyone or in every case.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「普遍地、人人皆然地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of applying to all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍性、通用性」。

entries.definition: Everything that exists, literally turned into one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，字面即「合为一体」。

entries.definition: A place of higher learning, once a whole community of scholars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学」，原指学者的全体团体。

entries.definition: The belief that a principle holds for everyone everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍主义」，认为某原则对天下所有人成立。

entries.definition: True in most cases but allowing exceptions; weaker than universal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一般的」，多数情形成立但允许例外，比 universal 弱。

entries.definition: Covering the whole world in space or reach.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全球的」，指在空间或影响上覆盖整个世界。

entries.definition: Found over a large area or among many people, but not necessarily all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广泛的」，地域或人群范围大，但不一定涵盖全部。

entries.definition: Shared by many or occurring often; it makes no claim about everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「共同的、常见的」，不主张对人人成立。

entries.definition: Broad in taste or interest, or universal in the older sense; formal and rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广泛的、普遍的」，较正式而少见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin pieces, one and turn, and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个拉丁部件「一」与「转」，以及这个词真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one and verse is to turn: turned into one, so everything is inside.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，verse 是「转」：转成一整个，所以一切都在里面。

normal.en: A universal truth holds for everyone, without exceptions.
normal.cn: 普遍真理对每人都成立，没有例外。

normal.en: A universal charger replaces a bag of cables.
normal.cn: 通用充电器能替掉一包线。

normal.en: University and universe share the root: one whole of students, one whole of things.
normal.cn: university 与 universe 共享词根：学生的整体，与万物的整体。

normal.en: Universal approval means not one hand stayed down.
normal.cn: 一致赞同意味着没有一只手没举起来。

abstract.en: Picture a dome wide enough to cover every town at once: whatever stands outside it is, by definition, an exception.
abstract.cn: 想象一个宽到能同时罩住每座城镇的圆顶：站在外面的事物按定义就是例外。

abstract.en: To call a rule universal is a strong claim; one counterexample is enough to break it.
abstract.cn: 称一条规律为普遍的是很强的断言：一个反例就足以打破它。

abstract.en: The word gathers a whole world into one turning point, which is why it can cover laws and people alike.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一整个世界收进同一个转折点，因此它既能盖住规律，也能盖住人。

examples.en: Music is often called a universal language.
examples.cn: 音乐常被称为一种通用语言。

examples.en: Access to clean water should be a universal right.
examples.cn: 获得干净的水应当是一项普遍权利。

examples.en: The plan met with universal support at the council meeting.
examples.cn: 这项计划在议会上得到了全体支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃索」——优尼把沃索全部转进一个圈：普遍的、全体的

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 vertere「转动」构成的 universus「合成一个的、整个的」，晚期拉丁语 universalis「属于全体的」经法语进入英语；由「全体」引申出普遍、通用与宇宙等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of universal all describe one reach: a whole gathered into one, whether it is all people, all cases, all of space, a shared concept, or a vote without exception.
sensesIntro.cn: universal 的五个义项都描述同一种覆盖：把整体收成一个，无论那是所有人、所有情形、整个空间、共有概念，还是无一例外的表决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vast dome that encloses every place and leaves nothing outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个巨大的圆顶罩住每一处，什么都不留在外面。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: a feeling or truth shared by everyone.
branches.cn: 人群线：人人都共有的感受或真理。

branches.en: THE TOOL: one design that fits every case.
branches.cn: 工具线：一种设计适用于每一种情形。

branches.en: THE COSMOS: the reach extends to all of space.
branches.cn: 宇宙线：覆盖范围扩展到整个空间。

branches.en: THE CONCEPT: philosophy names what many things share.
branches.cn: 概念线：哲学为众多事物共有之物命名。

branches.en: THE VOTE: nobody is left outside the agreement.
branches.cn: 表决线：没有人被留在同意之外。

intro.en: Universal is a Latin compound plus an adjective ending, with English suffixes for its family.
intro.cn: universal 是一个拉丁语复合词加形容词词尾，家族成员用英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Unus, vertere and universus are all recorded, and universalis is recorded in late Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus、vertere、universus 均有记录，universalis 见于晚期拉丁语。

items.example: The prefix gathers everything into one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一切收进一个。

items.example: The root gives the turning towards one.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「转向一」的意思。
它把 universus 变成 universal。

definition_zh: 宇宙；万物；领域；范围；全体
definition_en: all of space and everything in it, or a particular area of interest or activity
core_image: 无数星点在一个不断向外膨胀的巨大黑暗球体里旋转，全部合成一个整体
scene: 天文台的圆顶在夜里滑开，望远镜对准一片几乎看不见的星云。Astronomers say the universe is still expanding today.
sceneCN: 这里 universe 是「宇宙」（第 1 个义项：整个空间及其中的一切）；句意为天文学家说宇宙如今仍在膨胀。全部星点合为一体的那一整片，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源，义为「普遍的；全体的」
由 universal 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地」
与本词同源，义为「大学」，原指学者的全体
由 univers 加 -ology 与 -ical 构成，义为「宇宙学的」

senses.title: All of space and matter
senses.definition: all of space and everything in it, taken as one whole
senses.definitionCN: 整个空间及其中的一切，被视为一个整体
senses.example: Light from the farthest galaxies has travelled most of the age of the universe.
senses.exampleCN: 最远星系的光已经走了宇宙年龄的大部分时间。
senses.why: Unus is one and versus is turned: all things turned into a single whole.
senses.whyCN: unus 是「一」，versus 是「转」：万物转成一个整体。

senses.title: A field of activity
senses.definition: a particular area of knowledge, activity, or interest with its own laws
senses.definitionCN: 具有自身规律的一个特定知识、活动或兴趣领域
senses.example: In the universe of small business, cash flow is the first rule.
senses.exampleCN: 在小型企业的领域里，现金流是第一法则。
senses.why: A field so large that it has its own laws is felt to be a whole, and the name for the whole is applied to it.
senses.whyCN: 一个大到有自身法则的范围会被感觉成一个整体，而表示整体的名称就被用到它身上。

senses.title: The whole set of something
senses.definition: the complete collection of a kind of thing, without exception
senses.definitionCN: 某一类事物的完整集合，没有例外
senses.example: The survey tried to cover the universe of public libraries in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查试图覆盖全国公共图书馆的全体。
senses.why: Counting every member and stopping at nothing gives the same total that the word first meant.
senses.whyCN: 把每个成员都数上而不留下任何例外，得到的就是这个词最初所指的那个总和。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a set of people with shared work or interests, such as the art world
senses.definitionCN: 因工作或兴趣相同而聚成的一群人，如艺术界
senses.example: Her paintings are well known inside the fashion universe.
senses.exampleCN: 她的画作在时尚圈里广为人知。
senses.why: People who share a trade form a closed circle, and a closed circle is a small universe of its own.
senses.whyCN: 同行的人形成一个封闭的圈子，而封闭的圈子本身就是一个小小的宇宙。

senses.title: A world of one's own
senses.definition: an imagined or invented world, as in a fictional or parallel universe
senses.definitionCN: 想象或虚构出来的世界，如小说世界或平行宇宙
senses.example: Every novel creates a small universe with its own weather and laws.
senses.exampleCN: 每部小说都创造出一个有自己的天气与法则的小世界。
senses.why: If a whole needs nothing outside itself, an invented one can be complete too, and the word is lent to fiction.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个整体无需外物即可自足，那么虚构的整体也可以完整，这个词便借给了小说。

intro.en: Universe comes straight from a Latin adjective meaning turned into one, and became a noun in French before English.
intro.cn: universe 直接来自一个意为「合成一个」的拉丁语形容词，在法语中先成为名词，再进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one and vertere meant to turn; universus described many things turned into one whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，vertere 意为「转动」；universus 表示许多事物转成一个整体。

items.en: The neuter form universum was used as a noun for the whole of things.
items.cn: 其中性形式 universum 被用作名词，指万物的全体。

items.en: Old French univers took the noun for the totality of creation, and used it for a whole community as well.
items.cn: 古法语 univers 接纳了这个名词，指造物的全体，也用来指一个完整的团体。

items.en: English adopted universe for the whole of created things, earth and heavens together.
items.cn: 英语以 universe 指被造万物的全体，天地合在一起。

items.en: Astronomy redrew the word as all of space and time, and everyday speech borrowed it for any large field or circle.
items.cn: 天文学把这个词界定为整个空间与时间，日常言语又借它指任何大的领域或圈子。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same one-and-turn root; the near-meaning group gathers words for totalities of different kinds.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「合一」词根上的词；近义组收表示不同类型整体的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning true of everyone or everything.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「普遍的、全体的」。

entries.definition: A place of higher learning; once a whole guild of scholars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学」，原指学者的整个行会。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning by all or in every case.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「普遍地」。

entries.definition: The plural, used for imagined or parallel worlds.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，多用于虚构世界或平行宇宙。

entries.definition: Varied and unlike each other; it contains vers but no one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，含 vers 但不含「一」。

entries.definition: The universe seen as an ordered, harmonious whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，强调其有秩序的和谐整体。

entries.definition: All that exists, seen as made by a creator.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「造物、万物」，带有被创造的含义。

entries.definition: The earth and its people, or a particular sphere of life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「世界」，也可指某个生活领域。

entries.definition: A kingdom or a distinct area of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「领域、王国」，指一个独立的范围。

entries.definition: One of the large systems of stars; only a part of the universe.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星系」，只是宇宙的一部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin pieces of the word and the phrases it appears in today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的拉丁部件，以及它今天常见的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one and verse is turn: the whole of things turned into one.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，verse 是「转」：万物转成一个。

normal.en: The universe is still expanding, so the word names something it cannot hold still.
normal.cn: 宇宙仍在膨胀，因此这个词命名的东西无法静止。

normal.en: University carries the same root: one whole community of scholars.
normal.cn: university 有同一词根：一整个学者的团体。

normal.en: A parallel universe is invented; the fashion universe is merely a large circle.
normal.cn: 平行宇宙是虚构的；时尚界只是一大圈人。

normal.en: The universe of libraries means every library, counted together.
normal.cn: 图书馆的全体指把所有图书馆加在一起。

abstract.en: Picture every star turned towards one centre: the word started as an act of gathering, not a place.
abstract.cn: 想象所有星辰都朝向同一个中心：这个词起初是收拢的动作，而不是一个地点。

abstract.en: Any field large enough to have its own rules gets called a universe, because it is whole inside itself.
abstract.cn: 任何大到有自己规则的领域都会被称作一个宇宙，因为它在内部自成整体。

abstract.en: The word is an answer to a question: what is there, if you count everything at once.
abstract.cn: 这个词回答的是一个问题：如果把所有东西一次数完，那里有什么。

examples.en: Scientists still argue about how the universe began.
examples.cn: 科学家们仍在争论宇宙是如何开始的。

examples.en: In the universe of online shops, speed of delivery decides everything.
examples.cn: 在网络商店这个领域里，送货速度决定一切。

examples.en: The novel builds a universe where people can hear each other's thoughts.
examples.cn: 这部小说构建了一个人们能听见彼此心思的世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃斯」——优尼把沃斯整个转成一团：宇宙、全体

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 vertere「转动」构成的 universus「合成一个的、整个的」，其中性形式 universum 作名词指万物全体，经古法语 univers 进入英语，近代天文学用来指整个空间与时间。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of universe all name a whole gathered into one: all of space, a field with its own rules, a complete set, a circle of people, or an imagined world.
sensesIntro.cn: universe 的五个义项都在命名被收成一个的整体：整个空间、自成一体的领域、完整的集合、一圈人，或虚构的世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: countless stars turning inside one vast sphere of darkness.
core.cn: 核心意象：无数星点在同一个巨大黑暗球体里旋转。

branches.en: THE COSMOS: space and every object in it, taken together.
branches.cn: 宇宙线：空间及其中的每一个物体，合在一起。

branches.en: THE FIELD: one area of activity with its own rules.
branches.cn: 领域线：一个有自身规则的特定活动范围。

branches.en: THE SET: every member of a kind, without exception.
branches.cn: 集合线：某一类里的每个成员，没有例外。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE: a group of people who share a world.
branches.cn: 圈子线：共享同一个世界的一群人。

branches.en: THE INVENTION: fiction builds small universes of its own.
branches.cn: 虚构线：小说造出自己的一方小宇宙。

intro.en: Universe is a two-piece Latin compound, and the rest of its family is made with English suffixes.
intro.cn: universe 是两段组成的拉丁语复合词，家族其余成员由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Unus, vertere and universus are all recorded, and universum appears as a noun in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus、vertere、universus 均有记录，universum 在拉丁语中作名词使用。

items.example: It closes the Latin adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁语形容词收成名词。

definition_zh: 大学；综合性大学；大学校园
definition_en: a large school for higher education where students study for degrees and research is done
core_image: 一片古老的院落里，几栋教学楼、图书馆与宿舍围成一圈，学生抱着书穿过草坪
scene: 九月清晨，新生拖着箱子在门口停下，抬头看着门楣上刻着校名的石碑。She chose this university because of its astronomy department.
sceneCN: 这里 university 是「大学」（第 1 个义项：授予学位并进行研究的高等学校）；句意为她因为天文系而选择了这所大学。门口刻着校名的那片院落，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 大学全体师生（集合用法）

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源，义为「普遍的；全体的」
与本词同源，义为「宇宙；全体」
由本词加 -arian 构成，义为「大学的；大学成员的」
由 inter- 加本词构成，义为「校际的」

senses.title: A place that grants degrees
senses.definition: an institution for higher education that awards degrees and carries out research
senses.definitionCN: 授予学位并进行研究的高等教育机构
senses.example: She teaches chemistry at a university in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她在北方的一所大学教化学。
senses.why: Universitas first meant any whole body of people; the guild of teachers and students became this kind of school.
senses.whyCN: universitas 最初指任何一个人的整体；教师与学生的行会后来成了这种学校。

senses.title: The buildings and grounds
senses.definition: the buildings and grounds of such an institution, taken as a place
senses.definitionCN: 这样一所机构的建筑与场地，被当作一个地方
senses.example: The whole university was quiet during the summer holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 暑假期间整个校园都很安静。
senses.why: The abstract body of scholars became a physical place on a map.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的学者团体变成了地图上一个实在的地方。

senses.title: Its members together
senses.definition: all the students and teachers of the institution as a single community
senses.definitionCN: 把一所院校的学生与教师视为一个共同体
senses.example: The university voted to change the name of its main hall.
senses.exampleCN: 全校投票决定更改主楼的名字。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives: a university is still a group of people, not only walls.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义仍在：大学仍然是一群人，而不只是墙。

senses.title: The idea of higher learning
senses.definition: used generally of higher education as a stage of life or a system
senses.definitionCN: 泛指高等教育这一阶段或这一体系
senses.example: Going to university changes how a young person reads the world.
senses.exampleCN: 上大学会改变一个年轻人看世界的方式。
senses.why: British usage leaves out the article to name the stage itself rather than a building.
senses.whyCN: 英式用法省略冠词，指的是这个阶段本身而不是一栋建筑。

senses.title: Life as a school
senses.definition: in fixed phrases such as the university of life, experience treated as an education
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the university of life 等固定说法，把经历当作一种教育
senses.example: He never finished school, but the university of life taught him plenty.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有念完书，但社会这所大学教了他很多。
senses.why: The word becomes a metaphor: anything that teaches at length is granted its name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了比喻：凡是长期教人的东西都被赋予它的名字。

intro.en: University began as a Latin word for any whole body of people, and narrowed to the guild of scholars.
intro.cn: university 起初是拉丁语里指任何人的整体的词，后来收窄为学者的行会。

items.en: Universus meant turned into one, whole, and universitas meant the whole of a group.
items.cn: 拉丁语 universus 意为「合成一个的、整个的」，universitas 意为「一个团体的全体」。

items.en: In the Middle Ages universitas was used for any guild or corporation, including that of teachers and students.
items.cn: 中世纪时 universitas 可指任何行会或法人团体，也包括教师与学生的行会。

items.en: French université was applied specifically to the scholars' guild and the school it ran.
items.cn: 法语 université 专门用来指学者的行会及其所办的学校。

items.en: English took university in the fourteenth century for a school of higher learning with its own rules.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 university 指有自身规章的高等学校。

items.en: The word spread with modern degree systems, and British usage dropped the article in go to university.
items.cn: 随着现代学位制度普及，这个词流传开来，英式用法在 go to university 中省略了冠词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same whole-body root; the near-meaning group gathers names for institutions of learning.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「整体」词根上的词；近义组收各类教育机构的名称。

entries.definition: The adjective for what applies to all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「普遍的」。

entries.definition: All of space and matter; the root word of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，是这一词族的根词。

entries.definition: The quality of holding for everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍性」。

entries.definition: The plural, used for several institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指多所大学。

entries.definition: Variety and difference; close in sound but built on another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性」，读音相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: A smaller institution or a part of a university; often grants diplomas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院」，规模较小或是大学的一部分。

entries.definition: A school for a special field, or a learned society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专科院校、学会」，多用于特定领域。

entries.definition: An organization for research or teaching in one field.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、研究所」，多指某一领域的研究或教学机构。

entries.definition: A school for technical and applied subjects; in Britain often now a university.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理工学院」，在英国如今多已成为大学。

entries.definition: A general word for any place of teaching, including primary ones.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学校」，泛指任何教学场所，包括小学。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the old sense of a whole body of people and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词「一群人的整体」的古老意义，以及它常见的搭配。

normal.en: Universitas meant any whole guild: a university is still a whole body of teachers and students.
normal.cn: universitas 指任何完整的行会：大学仍是教师与学生的整体。

normal.en: In British English people say go to university with no article.
normal.cn: 英式英语说 go to university，不加冠词。

normal.en: University student, university degree, university entrance: the word mainly works as an attributive.
normal.cn: university student、university degree、university entrance：这个词多作定语。

normal.en: The plural is universities, with the y turned to ie.
normal.cn: 复数是 universities，y 变为 ie。

normal.en: The university of life is a school without walls.
normal.cn: the university of life 是一所没有围墙的学校。

abstract.en: Picture a gate carved with a name: everyone who walks through becomes part of one body.
abstract.cn: 想象镌刻着校名的大门：走进来的人都成为一个整体的一部分。

abstract.en: The building and the community share one word, because the oldest sense is the people, not the stones.
abstract.cn: 建筑与共同体共用同一个词，因为最古老的意义是人而不是石头。

abstract.en: A university is a place that keeps knowledge alive by passing it on.
abstract.cn: 大学是一个靠传递而让知识活下来的地方。

examples.en: He studied law at a university in Beijing.
examples.cn: 他在北京的一所大学读法律。

examples.en: Most students live on campus during their first year at university.
examples.cn: 多数学生上大学的头一年住在校内。

examples.en: The university has three libraries and a small museum.
examples.cn: 这所大学有三个图书馆和一座小博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃西提」——优尼沃西一提校名，人人都成了整体：大学

root: 源自拉丁语 universus「合成一个的、整个的」所生的 universitas「团体的全体」，中世纪指任何行会，包括师生行会；经古法语 université 进入英语，专指有自身规章的高等学校。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of university all rest on one old idea: a whole body of people. That body became a school, then a place, then a stage of life, then a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: university 的五个义项都立在一个古老观念上：一群人的整体。这个整体成了学校，又成了地方、人生阶段，最后成了比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of old buildings around a lawn, with a carved name above the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片古老建筑围着草坪，门楣上刻着校名。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the guild became an institution that grants degrees.
branches.cn: 学校线：行会变成了授予学位的机构。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the institution has walls, lawns and libraries.
branches.cn: 地点线：这所机构有墙、草坪与图书馆。

branches.en: THE MEMBERS: the oldest sense, all its students and teachers together.
branches.cn: 成员线：最古老的意义，全体师生合在一起。

branches.en: THE STAGE: going to university names a period of life.
branches.cn: 阶段线：上大学指的是人生的一段时期。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any long teacher is granted the name.
branches.cn: 比喻线：任何长期的教导者都被赋予这个名字。

intro.en: University is a Latin compound with the Latin suffix -tas, which becomes -ty in English.
intro.cn: university 是带拉丁语后缀 -tas 的复合词，该后缀在英语中变为 -ty。

latinIntro.en: Universus and universitas are both recorded, and the suffix -tas is the standard Latin way to make a noun of quality.
latinIntro.cn: universus 与 universitas 均有记录，-tas 是拉丁语构成性质名词的标准后缀。

items.example: The prefix gathers the group into one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把人群收成一个。

items.example: The root gives the turning to one side.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出朝向一边转的意思。
它把 universitas 变成 university。

items.meaning: the whole of a body, a guild

items.example: The sense that produced the school.
items.exampleCN: 生出了这种学校的那个义项。

latinEntries.meaning: the whole of a body, a guild

definition_zh: 未知的；不著名的；陌生的；未知的事物；无名者
definition_en: not known, not identified, or not famous, or a person or thing that is not known
core_image: 一张地图的边缘渐渐变淡，最后化成一片没有标注的空白，只写着「未探明」
scene: 侦探把照片翻过来，背面没有一个字，只有一枚模糊的指纹。The identity of the caller remains unknown.
sceneCN: 这里 unknown 是「未知的、不为人知的」（第 1 个义项：尚不被知道）；句意为来电者的身份仍然不明。地图上那片没被标注的空白，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由古英语 uncuð 一类形式经 know 加 -able 构成，义为「不可知的」
由 unknown 的词干加 -ingly 构成，义为「不知不觉地」
本词的复数，义为「若干未知因素」
本词去掉 un-，义为「已知的；著名的」

senses.title: Not known at all
senses.definition: not known to anyone, or not yet discovered or understood
senses.definitionCN: 尚不为人所知，或尚未被发现与理解
senses.example: The cause of the fire is still unknown.
senses.exampleCN: 起火的原因仍不清楚。
senses.why: Un- denies and know supplies the knowing: the fact has not been reached by any mind.
senses.whyCN: un- 表示否定，know 提供「知道」：这个事实还没有被任何头脑触及。

senses.title: Not identified
senses.definition: not recognized or identified, as of a person, a name, or a source
senses.definitionCN: 不能辨认或确认，如某个人、某个名字或某个来源
senses.example: Police are searching for an unknown man seen near the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在寻找一名在银行附近被看到的身份不明男子。
senses.why: Here the thing exists but its label is missing; the gap is in identification.
senses.whyCN: 这里事物存在，缺的是标签；空缺在身份辨认上。

senses.title: Not famous
senses.definition: not well known to the public, though perhaps respected by a few
senses.definitionCN: 不为公众所知，虽然可能被少数人看重
senses.example: The painting was bought for a small sum from an unknown artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画以很低的价钱从一位不出名的画家那里买来。
senses.why: Reputation is a kind of knowing held by many; if few know you, you are unknown.
senses.whyCN: 名声是许多人所持有的一种知道；知道你的少，你就是不为人知。

senses.title: The unknown as a whole
senses.definition: with the, the part of the world or of knowledge not yet explored or understood
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指世界或知识中尚未被探索与理解的部分
senses.example: Explorers in those years were drawn to the unknown.
senses.exampleCN: 那些年的探险者被未知吸引。
senses.why: An adjective of state becomes a noun for the whole region no one has entered.
senses.whyCN: 表示状态的形容词转成了名词，指没人进入过的那一整片区域。

senses.title: A person without a name
senses.definition: with a, someone whose name is not known, as in an unknown soldier
senses.definitionCN: 与 a 连用，指名字不为所知的人，如无名战士
senses.example: A stone in the square honours the unknown who fell in the war.
senses.exampleCN: 广场上的一块石头纪念战争中阵亡的无名者。
senses.why: The word names the person by what is missing, which is why it can honour them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以「缺少的东西」来命名人，因此它能够用来致敬。

intro.en: Unknown began as a native Old English compound and has kept the same shape for a thousand years.
intro.cn: unknown 起初是古英语本土复合词，一千年来形式几乎未变。

items.en: Un- denied and cnāwan meant to know; the compound uncūþ covered what was not known.
items.cn: un- 是否定前缀，cnāwan 意为「知道」；复合词 uncūþ 指所不知道的事物。

items.en: Norse influence helped know and its forms settle as the everyday words of England.
items.cn: 诺尔斯语影响使 know 及其种种形式成为英格兰日常用语。

items.en: The form settled as unknow(e)n, spelled closer to the modern word.
items.cn: 中古英语中形式固定为 unknow(e)n，拼写接近现代。

items.en: The word spread from facts to people, becoming a title for the anonymous, as in the unknown soldier.
items.cn: 这个词从事实扩展到人，成为无名者的称谓，如无名战士。

items.en: Science and mathematics made the noun common, as in unknowns in an equation.
items.cn: 科学与数学使名词用法普及，如方程中的未知数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words in un- and forms of know; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is not familiar or not certain.
