note.cn: 形近组收其他以 un- 构成的词以及 know 的各种形式；近义组收表示不熟悉或不确定的形容词。

entries.definition: The adjective for what is recognized or widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已知的、著名的」，与本词相反。

entries.definition: Beyond any possibility of being known.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可知的」，根本无从得知。

entries.definition: Without being aware of it; the word describes a person's action.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不知不觉地」，描述人的行为。

entries.definition: Not known because not met before; it stresses lack of acquaintance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不熟悉的」，强调没有接触过。

entries.definition: Going without being seen or heeded.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未被注意到的」。

entries.definition: Not easy to understand; the facts exist but are dim.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不清楚的」，事实存在但模糊。

entries.definition: Of a person whose name is not given; formal and common in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「匿名的」，较正式，多用于书面。

entries.definition: Little known, or hard to see; often used of writers and words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「鲜为人知的、晦涩的」，多用于作者与词语。

entries.definition: Not settled or sure; it describes doubt rather than absence of knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不确定的」，描述怀疑而非知识的缺失。

entries.definition: Strange and hard to explain, often with a feeling of secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「神秘的」，带有秘密的气氛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus know structure and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 know 的朴素结构，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and know is to know: literally not known.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，know 是「知道」：字面就是不被知道。

normal.en: Unknown to me means I was never told.
normal.cn: unknown to me 意为从来没人告诉过我。

normal.en: The unknown soldier is honoured precisely because his name is missing.
normal.cn: 无名战士之所以受纪念，恰恰因为名字缺失。

normal.en: In an equation the unknowns are the letters you must solve for.
normal.cn: 方程中的未知数就是你要解出的那些字母。

normal.en: The opposite is simply known.
normal.cn: 其反面就是 known。

abstract.en: Picture the edge of an old map fading into blank paper: what is missing is not nothing, but unwritten space.
abstract.cn: 想象旧地图的边缘淡成空白纸：缺的不是「没有」，而是尚未写下的空间。

abstract.en: Unknown is a word about the limits of a mind, not about the thing itself.
abstract.cn: unknown 说的是头脑的界限，而不是事物本身。

abstract.en: Every discovery begins as an unknown that nobody had yet named.
abstract.cn: 每一项发现最初都是一个还没人命名过的未知。

examples.en: The exact number of birds on the island is unknown.
examples.cn: 岛上鸟的确切数量未知。

examples.en: An unknown woman returned the lost wallet to the desk.
examples.cn: 一位不知名的女子把丢失的钱包交到了前台。

examples.en: They set out into the unknown with three weeks of food.
examples.cn: 他们带着三周的食物走向未知。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的弄恩」——安对此弄不明白，全然不知：未知的

root: 由否定前缀 un- 与古英语动词 cnāwan「知道」（今 know）构成，古英语作 uncūþ，中古英语写作 unknow(e)n；由「不被知道」扩展到身份不明、不出名，并名词化为未知之物与无名者。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unknown all mark a gap in knowing: a fact not reached, a face not identified, a name not famous, a region unexplored, or a person without a name.
sensesIntro.cn: unknown 的五个义项都标记认知上的空缺：未被触及的事实、未被辨认的面孔、不出名的名字、未被探索的区域，或没有名字的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the edge of a map fading into blank paper with nothing written there.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图边缘淡成白纸，上面什么都没有写。

branches.en: THE FACT: something true that nobody has found out yet.
branches.cn: 事实线：确实存在却还没人查明的事情。

branches.en: THE FACE: the person is present, the identity is missing.
branches.cn: 面孔线：人在那里，身份却是空白。

branches.en: THE NAME: few people know him, though he may deserve it.
branches.cn: 名字线：知道他的人很少，尽管他可能值得被知道。

branches.en: THE REGION: the noun names the whole unexplored part.
branches.cn: 区域线：名词化后指整片未被探索之处。

branches.en: THE UNNAMED: honouring those whose names were never recorded.
branches.cn: 无名线：用来致敬那些名字从未被记下的人。

intro.en: Unknown is entirely native: a Germanic negative prefix on an Old English verb, with no Latin element at all.
intro.cn: unknown 完全是本土构造：日耳曼语否定前缀加古英语动词，不含任何拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin in this word; the table lists later Latin-based synonyms that cover the same gap.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁成分；下表列出后世以拉丁语为源、指同样空缺的近义词。

items.example: The verb supplies the act that is missing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供缺失的那个动作。

items.example: The older native form of know.
The oldest recorded form of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最古老的记录形式。
一个正式的拉丁语来源近义词。

definition_zh: 除非；如果不；除非在……情况下
definition_en: except if; used to say that something will happen only if another thing does not happen
core_image: 一个岔路口立着一块牌子：除非走左边，否则到不了目的地；右边是一条被挡住的路
scene: 教练在雨天早晨对队员说，只有雨停才训练，否则全体在馆里看录像。We will not play outside unless the rain stops by noon.
sceneCN: 这里 unless 是「除非」（第 1 个义项：表示只有在某条件不成立时才发生）；句意为除非中午前雨停，否则我们不在外面踢球。路口那块牌子划出的唯一通路，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 除非；如果不（引导条件从句）
除……之外（少见，多见于书面）
除非在……的情况下（与 not 连用表双重否定）

collocations.zh: 除非……否则什么也不会发生

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「带 unless 从句的」
由古英语 þy læs þe 缩合而成，义为「以免」，是 unless 的老近亲
与本词同源，义为「较少的」，构成 unless 的后半

senses.title: Except if
senses.definition: except if; a condition that alone can change the result
senses.definitionCN: 「除非」；唯一能够改变结果的那个条件
senses.example: You cannot enter unless you show your ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 除非出示门票，否则你不能进场。
senses.why: Unless is a compressed on less: the case you name is the single exception to the statement.
senses.whyCN: unless 是 on less 的压缩：你提出的那种情形是对这句话的唯一例外。

senses.title: Only in that case
senses.definition: used after a negative or in a question to mean only if
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句或疑问句之后，意为「只有在……才」
senses.example: I will not agree unless the whole plan is explained first.
senses.exampleCN: 除非先把整个计划解释清楚，否则我不会同意。
senses.why: With not in front, the exception becomes the one door left open.
senses.whyCN: 前面加了 not，这个例外就成了唯一还开着的门。

senses.title: Except for
senses.definition: in older or formal prose, except for a thing just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在较早或正式的书面语中，指「除了刚提到的某物」
senses.example: Nothing was left of the house unless the stone steps.
senses.exampleCN: 除了那几级石阶，这座房子什么也没有剩下。
senses.why: The very old prepositional use keeps the plain sense of less as leaving something out.
senses.whyCN: 很古老的介词用法保留着 less「除去」的朴素含义。

senses.title: In fixed legal phrases
senses.definition: in clauses such as unless otherwise stated, the rule applies except where noted
senses.definitionCN: 在 unless otherwise stated 一类条款中，表示除注明处之外规则一律适用
senses.example: The fee is paid yearly unless otherwise agreed in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 除非另有书面约定，费用按年支付。
senses.why: Contracts need a single word for the written exception, and this is that word.
senses.whyCN: 合同需要一个词专门表示书面的例外，用的就是这个词。

senses.title: Doubled for emphasis
senses.definition: in the phrase unless and until, meaning not before at the earliest
senses.definitionCN: 在 unless and until 这一说法中，意为「最早也要到……才行」
senses.example: The office stays closed unless and until the roof is repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 除非并且直到屋顶修好，办公室才会重新开放。
senses.why: Two limiters side by side make the condition sound impossible to soften.
senses.whyCN: 两个限定词并排，让这个条件听起来无从通融。

intro.en: Unless is a worn-down phrase rather than a word built from parts: on less, meaning on a lesser condition.
intro.cn: unless 不是由词缀构成，而是一个磨短了的短语：on less，意为「在较小的条件下」。

items.en: The preposition on and the comparative lǣssa, less, stood side by side as on lǣssan, on a lesser condition.
items.cn: 介词 on 与比较级 lǣssa（较少）并列为 on lǣssan，意为「在较小的条件下」。

items.en: The phrase shrank to on lesse and then to unless, losing the space and then the o.
items.cn: 这个短语缩为 on lesse，再缩为 unless，先丢了空格，又丢了 o。

items.en: By the fourteenth century unless was used as a conjunction before a clause.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，unless 已用作引导从句的连词。

items.en: Lest, from a parallel phrase, kept the older meaning of avoiding something, and the two words divided the work.
items.cn: 由类似短语来的 lest 保留了「以免」的旧义，两个词于是各司其职。

items.en: Modern contracts fixed unless otherwise stated as a standard clause formula.
items.cn: 现代合同把 unless otherwise stated 固化为标准条款用语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers negatives and near forms in un- or less; the near-meaning group gathers conjunctions of condition that differ in strength.
note.cn: 形近组收以 un- 或 less 构成的否定词与近形词；近义组收表示条件的连词，力度不同。

entries.definition: Up to the time that; it names a moment, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「直到」，指时间点而非条件。

entries.definition: About, regarding; close in sound to the old prepositional use only.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于」。

entries.definition: For fear that; the older partner of unless.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「以免」，是 unless 较早的搭档词。

entries.definition: In spite of that; it contains less but means despite, not except.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「然而、不过」，含 less 但意为转折而非例外。

entries.definition: Nevertheless; it contains less but means in spite of that.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「尽管如此」，含 less 但意义不同。

entries.definition: The plain conditional with a negative; unless is its compressed form.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「如果不」，unless 是其压缩形式。

entries.definition: The full phrase behind unless, still used in careful speech.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「除非」，是 unless 的完整说法。

entries.definition: Only on the condition that; it states the condition positively.
entries.definitionCN: 连词短语，义为「只要」，从正面提出条件。

entries.definition: If not, or in other circumstances; often pairs with unless in clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「否则」，常与 unless 在条款中配合使用。

entries.definition: As a precaution because something might happen; not the same as unless.
entries.definitionCN: 连词短语，义为「以防」，与 unless 不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the worn-down on less behind the word and the clauses it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后磨短的 on less，以及它常出现的从句。

normal.en: Unless is on less in disguise: the one case on a lesser footing, the exception.
normal.cn: unless 是 on less 的变形：那个处于次要地位的唯一情形，就是例外。

normal.en: Unless you show your ticket, you cannot enter: the exception is the only open door.
normal.cn: unless you show your ticket 意为除非出示门票；例外就是唯一开着的门。

normal.en: Unless otherwise stated is the standard formula in contracts.
normal.cn: unless otherwise stated 是合同里的标准说法。

normal.en: Do not confuse unless with until: one is a condition, the other a time.
normal.cn: 不要把 unless 与 until 混用：一个是条件，一个是时间。

normal.en: Lest and unless once did the same work.
normal.cn: lest 与 unless 曾做同一份工作。

abstract.en: Picture a road with a single gate: unless is the gate, and nothing else lets you through.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只有一道门的路：unless 就是那道门，别的都通不过。

abstract.en: The word thinks in negatives: it names the only thing that can stop the statement from being true.
abstract.cn: 这个词用否定来思考：它指出唯一能让这句话不成立的事。

abstract.en: Every rule has a unless hidden in it, which is why contracts love the word.
abstract.cn: 每条规则里都藏着一个 unless，所以合同喜欢这个词。

examples.en: Do not call me unless it is urgent.
examples.cn: 除非有急事，否则别打电话给我。

examples.en: The meeting will go ahead unless the storm gets worse.
examples.cn: 除非暴风雨加剧，会议照常举行。

examples.en: Unless otherwise stated, all prices include tax.
examples.cn: 除非另有说明，所有价格均含税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱斯」——安说：除非莱斯先来，否则不开始：除非

root: 由中古英语短语 on lesse（在较小的条件下）缩合而成，源自 on 与比较级 lǣssa（较少）；十四世纪起作连词，与 lest 分工，现代又在合同里固定为 except 条件的标准说法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unless all name the one exception: the only case where the statement fails, whether spoken as a condition, a negative clause, an old preposition, a contract formula, or a doubled limiter.
sensesIntro.cn: unless 的五个义项都指那唯一的例外：这句话唯一不成立的情形，表现为条件、否定从句、古老介词、合同套语或叠用的限定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single open gate on an otherwise blocked road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被挡住的路上一道唯一开着的门。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: the named case alone changes what happens.
branches.cn: 例外线：只有被点出的那种情形改变结果。

branches.en: THE NEGATIVE: after not, the exception becomes the only way in.
branches.cn: 否定线：在 not 之后，例外成了唯一的进路。

branches.en: THE OLD PREPOSITION: except for a thing, in older prose.
branches.cn: 旧介词线：在较早的书面语中表示「除某物之外」。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: written rules need a word for the noted exception.
branches.cn: 合同线：书面规则需要一个词表示注明的例外。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE LIMIT: unless and until leaves no room to soften.
branches.cn: 双限线：unless and until 不给任何通融余地。

intro.en: This word has no affixes at all: it is a phrase worn down to six letters.
intro.cn: 这个词完全没有词缀：它是一个被磨短到六个字母的短语。

latinIntro.en: Nothing here is Latin; under this word sit the preposition on and an old comparative meaning less.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；这个词底下是介词 on 与一个意为「较少」的古老比较级。

items.example: It survives only as the hidden first sound.
items.exampleCN: 它只作为隐藏的第一个音留存。

items.example: It is the modern shape of lǣssa.
items.exampleCN: 它是 lǣssa 的现代形式。

items.example: The comparative inside the old phrase.
items.exampleCN: 旧短语里的那个比较级。

items.example: A parallel contraction from þy læs þe.
items.exampleCN: 由 þy læs þe 并行的缩合词。

items.example: A look-alike that keeps less visible.
items.exampleCN: 一个把 less 留在表面的形近词。

items.example: The final form of on lesse.
Two limiters side by side in legal English.
items.exampleCN: 法律英语中并排使用的两个限定词。

definition_zh: 不像；与……不同；和……不一样；（作形容词）不同的；不相像的
definition_en: different from, not similar to, or in contrast to someone or something
core_image: 两枚并排放着的贝壳：一枚细长有纹，一枚扁圆光滑，一眼就看得出不是一家
scene: 姐姐安静地读书，弟弟却一整天都在院子里拆东西，母亲常对客人说他们是完全不同的人。Unlike her brother, she has never broken a single cup.
sceneCN: 这里 unlike 是「与……不同、不像」（第 1 个义项：表示对比）；句意为和弟弟不同，她从未打碎过一只杯子。两枚并排放着却毫不相像的贝壳，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 不典型的；不像平常那样的
不像……那样（非标准，口语偶见）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「不太可能的」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「不相似、不同」
本词去掉 un-，义为「像；如同」
与本词同源，义为「相似的」，多作表语

senses.title: Different from
senses.definition: used to say that one person or thing is different from another
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示某个人或物与另一个不同
senses.example: Unlike his father, he has never enjoyed fishing.
senses.exampleCN: 与他父亲不同，他从来不喜欢钓鱼。
senses.why: The prefix denies likeness while still setting the two people side by side, so the comparison stays visible.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀否认相像，却仍把两个人并排放着，比较因此看得见。

senses.title: Not similar to in kind
senses.titleCN: 不相像的；不类似的（形容词）
senses.definition: not similar in appearance, character, or nature
senses.definitionCN: 在外观、性格或性质上不相像
senses.example: The two sisters are unlike in almost every way.
senses.exampleCN: 这对姐妹几乎在各方面都不相像。
senses.why: As an adjective the same word drops the second person and simply denies sameness in nature.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，同一个词不再针对第二个对象，只是单纯否认性质上的相同。

senses.title: Not like the usual
senses.definition: not typical of a person, so that it surprises those who know them
senses.definitionCN: 不像某人平时那样，因而让熟悉的人感到意外
senses.example: It is unlike her to arrive so late.
senses.exampleCN: 迟到这么久不像她的作风。
senses.why: The comparison is now between a person and their own usual self, which is why the word can sound like surprise.
senses.whyCN: 比较发生在一个人与自己平日的模样之间，因此这个词听起来带着惊讶。

senses.title: To point at a contrast
senses.definition: at the start of a clause, drawing a contrast with what follows
senses.definitionCN: 用于从句开头，与后文形成对比
senses.example: Unlike other cities, this one keeps its trams in the centre.
senses.exampleCN: 与别的城市不同，这座城市把有轨电车保留在市中心。
senses.why: At the head of a clause the preposition sets the second half of the sentence against the first.
senses.whyCN: 放在从句开头时，这个介词把句子的后半段与前半段对立起来。

senses.title: Unlike anything else
senses.definition: in the phrase unlike anything, stressing that no comparison is possible
senses.definitionCN: 在 unlike anything 这一说法中，强调无从比较
senses.example: The storm was unlike anything the village had seen.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴是村里人从未见过的。
senses.why: When the second term is anything, the comparison is denied altogether: nothing matches.
senses.whyCN: 当比较的另一项是 anything 时，比较被彻底取消：没有任何东西能相配。

intro.en: Unlike is the native negative prefix on an Old English word for what is like or alike.
intro.cn: unlike 是本土否定前缀加一个古英语表示「相似」的词。

items.en: Gelīc meant of the same form or body, from līc, a body; it became the modern like and alike.
items.cn: 古英语 gelīc 意为「形体相同的」，源于 līc（身体）；后演变为 like 与 alike。

items.en: The prefix un- was already used to deny such adjectives, as in ungelīc.
items.cn: 否定前缀 un- 早已用来否定这类形容词，如 ungelīc。

items.en: The word settled as unlike, and was used both as adjective and as preposition.
items.cn: 这个词固定为 unlike，既可作形容词也可作介词。

items.en: Unlike at the head of a clause became the standard way to open a contrast in written English.
items.cn: 在书面英语中，用 unlike 开头引出对比成了标准做法。

items.en: The derived unlikely took over the sense of not probable, leaving unlike to comparison alone.
items.cn: 派生词 unlikely 承担了「不太可能」的意思，unlike 则只保留比较义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in un- and like-alike forms; the near-meaning group gathers ways to mark contrast.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 与 like、alike 一族的词；近义组收表示对比的说法。

entries.definition: Not probable; it points to chance rather than similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不太可能的」，指机会而不指相似。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不相似、不同」。

entries.definition: Similar to, or in the same way as; the word without un-.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「像」，即去掉 un- 的词。

entries.definition: Similar to each other; usually after the verb be.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「相似的」，多作表语。

entries.definition: To not like something; close in shape but about feeling, not similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不喜欢」，形近而意义不同。

entries.definition: The plain and safest comparative phrase in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「与……不同」，正式写作中最稳妥。

entries.definition: Marks a sharp difference; more formal and heavier than unlike.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「与……形成对比」，较正式。

entries.definition: Used to turn the sentence towards an opposite case.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「相比之下」，用于转向相反的情形。

entries.definition: A conjunction joining two contrasted clauses in one sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「而」，在同一句中连接两个对比分句。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning not alike; formal and used of things, not people's habits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不相似的」，较正式，多用于物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus like structure and the contrast phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 like 的朴素结构，以及这个词出现的对比搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and like means similar: not similar to.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，like 表示「像」：不像。

normal.en: Unlike her brother, she never breaks a cup: the phrase opens a contrast.
normal.cn: unlike her brother 意为与她弟弟不同；这个短语一开头就摆出对比。

normal.en: Unlike means not like, and it is the opposite of like rather than of likely.
normal.cn: unlike 意为「不像」，反义是 like 而不是 likely。

normal.en: Alike takes no un-: the pair is like and unlike, alike and unalike.
normal.cn: alike 不加 un-：配对的是 like 与 unlike、alike 与 unalike。

normal.en: To call a person unlike their usual self is to stress that this is not their habit.
normal.cn: 用 unlike 说某人反常，就是强调这不像他平时的样子。

abstract.en: Picture two shells of the same weight but a different shape: the hand feels at once that they are not of one family.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚重量相同而形状不同的贝壳：手一摸就知道它们不是一家。

abstract.en: Unlike does not deny a relation; it denies sameness while keeping the comparison.
abstract.cn: unlike 不否认关系，它否认相同，同时保留比较。

abstract.en: Every contrast needs two things put side by side, and the word is the space between them.
abstract.cn: 每个对比都需要两样东西并排，这个词就是它们之间的那段距离。

examples.en: Unlike most of his friends, he walks to work every day.
examples.cn: 与他多数朋友不同，他每天走路上班。

examples.en: The twins are unlike in temperament but close in spirit.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎性情不同，感情却很好。

examples.en: It is unlike him to complain without a reason.
examples.cn: 无缘无故地抱怨不像他的为人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱克」——安和莱克完全不像：不像、与……不同

root: 由否定前缀 un- 与古英语 gelīc（形体相同的，源于 līc「身体」）构成，古英语已有 ungelīc；中古英语定型为 unlike，作形容词与介词，近代在句首成为引出对比的标准说法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unlike all deny sameness while keeping a comparison: two people, two things, one person and their usual self, two places, or one thing and everything else.
sensesIntro.cn: unlike 的五个义项都否认相同却保留比较：两个人、两样东西、一个人与其平时的样子、两个地方，或一样东西与其余一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two shells side by side, obviously not of one family.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚并排的贝壳，一眼就看得出不是一家。

branches.en: THE PAIR: one person set against another, as a preposition.
branches.cn: 对照线：一个人与另一个人相对，作介词。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the adjective says the two are not alike in nature.
branches.cn: 形状线：形容词说两者性质上并不相像。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a person unlike their usual self.
branches.cn: 习惯线：一个人不像平时的自己。

branches.en: THE OPENING: unlike at the head of a clause sets up the contrast.
branches.cn: 开头线：unlike 置于句首，摆出对比。

branches.en: THE UNMATCHED: unlike anything leaves nothing to compare with.
branches.cn: 无偶线：unlike anything 表示无从比较。

intro.en: Unlike is a native prefix on a native adjective, with English suffixes for the rest of the family.
intro.cn: unlike 是本土前缀加本土形容词，家族其余成员由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin here; the roots are Old English, and later Latin-based synonyms are listed only for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；词根是古英语，列出的拉丁语来源近义词仅供对照。

items.example: The ancestor of like and alike.
items.exampleCN: like 与 alike 的祖先。

items.example: Already recorded before the Norman period.
items.exampleCN: 诺曼征服之前已有记录。

definition_zh: 不太可能的；未必会发生的；不像是真的；不大可能成功的
definition_en: not probable, or not likely to happen, be true, or succeed
core_image: 一只骰子稳稳停在最小的那一面上，其余可能性都被压在下面看不见
scene: 天气预报说晚上有雨，可天上半点云也没有，邻居还是把晾着的被子收了。It is unlikely to rain before nightfall, but she folded the sheets anyway.
sceneCN: 这里 unlikely 是「不太可能的」（第 1 个义项：发生的机会很小）；句意为天黑前不太可能下雨，但她还是把床单收了。落在最小那一面的骰子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 不太可能的；未必发生的
不像是真的；难以置信的
不大可能成功的（人选、方案）
未必（少见，多见于旧用法）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -hood 构成，义为「不大可能；可能性低」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「不太可能的程度」
本词去掉 un-，义为「很可能的」
与本词同源，义为「不像、与……不同」

senses.title: Not probable
senses.definition: having little chance of happening or being true
senses.definitionCN: 发生或成真的机会很小
senses.example: It is unlikely that the shop will open before ten.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店十点前开门不大可能。
senses.why: The negative prefix lowers a chance instead of denying it: the word is a wager that the thing will not happen.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀把机会压低而不是彻底否认：这个词是在赌那件事不会发生。

senses.title: Hard to believe
senses.definition: seeming too strange to be true
senses.definitionCN: 显得太离奇而不像是真的
senses.example: He gave an unlikely excuse about losing his shoes on the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了一个离奇的说法，说鞋在公交车上丢了。
senses.why: Truth is only another kind of probability, so an excuse can be improbable in the same way a forecast is.
senses.whyCN: 「真实」只是另一种概率，所以一个借口可以像预报那样显得不大可能。

senses.title: Surprisingly placed
senses.definition: used before a noun for a place, person, or pairing that one would not expect
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指某地方、人物或组合是意料之外的
senses.example: A small bookshop in a quiet street became an unlikely meeting place for poets.
senses.exampleCN: 一条安静街道上的小书店成了诗人们意料之外的聚会处。
senses.why: Before a noun the word measures surprise: this place simply did not look like the probable one.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，这个词衡量的是意外程度：这个地方本来就不像那个「很可能」的地方。

senses.title: Not expected to succeed
senses.definition: said of a candidate or plan with little chance of winning or working
senses.definitionCN: 用于指胜算或成功率很小的人选或方案
senses.example: The team was an unlikely winner, but it reached the final.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍本来不被看好，却打进了决赛。
senses.why: Success is another event with a chance, so the same word serves people and plans.
senses.whyCN: 成功也是一件有几率的事，因此同一个词也可用于人与方案。

senses.title: With to and a verb
senses.titleCN: 后接 to 表示判断
senses.definition: in the pattern be unlikely to do, marking a prediction that something will not happen
senses.definitionCN: 在 be unlikely to do 这一句型中，表示某事不会发生的预测
senses.example: The old bridge is unlikely to last another winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老桥未必能再撑过一个冬天。
senses.why: The infinitive turns the chance into a forecast about a single future event.
senses.whyCN: 不定式把这个几率变成对某一件未来事情的预测。

intro.en: Unlikely is the negative of likely, which came from Old Norse and crossed the North Sea into English.
intro.cn: unlikely 是 likely 的否定形式，likely 来自古诺尔斯语，越过北海进入英语。

items.en: Líkr meant like or similar, and the Norse adverb líkligr added the sense of probable.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 líkr 意为「相像的」，其副词形 líkligr 又添了「可能」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed likely from Norse speakers and used it for what is probable or suitable.
items.cn: 英语从诺尔斯语使用者那里借来 likely，用来指可能或合适的。

items.en: Un- was added to make unlikely, first meaning not similar, later not probable.
items.cn: 加上 un- 构成 unlikely，最初意为「不相像」，后来转为「不太可能」。

items.en: The negative sense of probability pushed out the older sense of similarity.
items.cn: 概率上的否定义把较早的相似义挤了出去。

items.en: The pattern be unlikely to do became the standard way to express a negative forecast.
items.cn: be unlikely to do 成了表达否定预测的标准句型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in un- and likely forms; the near-meaning group gathers expressions of low probability.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 与 likely 一族的词；近义组收表示低可能性的说法。

entries.definition: Different from; it compares things rather than chances.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「与……不同」，比较的是事物而非机会。

entries.definition: Probable; the word without the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「很可能的」，即去掉否定前缀的词。

entries.definition: The noun for a low chance that something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不大可能」，指低概率。

entries.definition: The state of being improbable, or of not being alike.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不太可能」或「不相像」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in the same way, or also.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「同样地、也」。

entries.definition: Not probable; more formal and a little stronger than unlikely.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不大可能发生的」，比 unlikely 更正式、略强。

entries.definition: Uncertain and probably not true; it carries the speaker's doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可疑的」，带有说话人的怀疑。

entries.definition: Hard to believe because too distant from reality, of an idea or story.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「牵强的」，指说法离现实太远。

entries.definition: Of a chance, very small; it names the size of the chance itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「微小的」，用于机会，指其本身很小。

entries.definition: Looking as if it will not succeed; about prospects, not chances of truth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「前景不佳的」，指前途而非真伪。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus likely structure and the patterns the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 likely 的朴素结构，以及这个词常见的句型。

normal.en: Un- means not and likely means probable: not probable.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，likely 表示「可能」：不太可能。

normal.en: It is unlikely that is the full clause pattern; be unlikely to do is the short one.
normal.cn: it is unlikely that 是完整从句句型，be unlikely to do 是简短的。

normal.en: An unlikely hero is one nobody expected to win.
normal.cn: an unlikely hero 指没人料到会赢的英雄。

normal.en: Highly unlikely is the usual way to say almost impossible.
normal.cn: highly unlikely 是表示「几乎不可能」的常用说法。

normal.en: Do not mix it with unlike, which compares things.
normal.cn: 不要与 unlike 混用，后者比较事物。

abstract.en: Picture a die landing on its smallest edge: possible, but balanced against many other faces.
abstract.cn: 想象骰子停在其最小的棱面上：有可能，但与许多别的面相比很难。

abstract.en: Unlikely is a bet, not a denial: the thing may still happen, just rarely.
abstract.cn: unlikely 是下注而不是否认：事情仍可能发生，只是很少。

abstract.en: Every surprise begins as something unlikely, which is why the word can describe a hero.
abstract.cn: 每一个惊喜都以「不太可能」开始，所以这个词能用来形容英雄。

examples.en: She is unlikely to arrive before nine.
examples.cn: 她不太可能九点前到。

examples.en: It seems unlikely that the two sides will agree today.
examples.cn: 双方今天达成一致似乎不太可能。

examples.en: A village post office became an unlikely stage for the play.
examples.cn: 村里的邮局成了这出戏出乎意料的舞台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱克利」——安以为莱克利会来，结果多半不来：不太可能的

root: 由否定前缀 un- 加 likely 构成；likely 借自古诺尔斯语 líkligr，本义为「相像的」，中古英语里生出「可能的」义，unlikely 最初的「不相像」义后来让位给「不太可能」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unlikely all lower a chance: of happening, of being true, of fitting a place, of succeeding, or of lasting.
sensesIntro.cn: unlikely 的五个义项都在调低一种机会：发生的机会、成真的机会、与场合相称的机会、成功的机会、持续下去的机会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a die resting on its narrowest edge, other faces hidden below.
core.cn: 核心意象：骰子停在最窄的棱面上，别的面都压在下面看不见。

branches.en: THE CHANCE: the main sense, whether as a clause or with to.
branches.cn: 机会线：主要义项，可用从句或接 to。

branches.en: THE STORY: an excuse too strange to believe.
branches.cn: 说法线：一个离奇到难以相信的借口。

branches.en: THE SETTING: a place or pairing nobody would have chosen.
branches.cn: 场合线：没人会想到的地点或组合。

branches.en: THE OUTCOME: a team or plan given little hope.
branches.cn: 结果线：不被看好的队伍或方案。

branches.en: THE BET: even the word keeps some chance open.
branches.cn: 下注线：即使这个词也仍留着一线机会。

intro.en: Unlikely is a native prefix on a Norse-derived adjective, with English noun suffixes on top.
intro.cn: unlikely 是本土前缀加诺尔斯语来源的形容词，上面又长出一对英语名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin; the Latin-based cousins are listed only as near meanings.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是日耳曼语而非拉丁语；拉丁语来源的近义词只作为近义对照列出。

items.example: The prefix turns probable into improbable.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「可能」变成「不可能」。
最深处的词根意为「相像」。
它构成 likely 与 unlikely。

items.example: The English cousin of the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根上的英语近亲。

items.example: A formal synonym from Latin probare.
items.exampleCN: 源自拉丁语 probare 的正式近义词。

definition_zh: 卸货；卸下；退出子弹；倾诉（心事）；卸载（数据）
definition_en: to remove goods from a vehicle, to take bullets out of a gun, or to tell someone your worries
core_image: 卡车后挡板放下，几个工人把一箱箱货搬下来，车厢一点点变轻变空
scene: 货车在仓库门口倒车停稳，司机跳下来掀开帆布，晨光里全是灰尘。They began to unload the boxes at six in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 unload 是「卸货、卸下」（第 1 个义项：把货物从车船上搬走）；句意为他们早上六点开始卸箱子。车厢一点点被搬空的那种变轻感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 倾诉；把心里的负担说出来

collocations.zh: 向某人倾诉；把情绪发泄到某人身上

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「卸货；卸载」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「未装货的；未装弹的」
本词去掉 un-，义为「装载；装填」
由 load 加 -er 构成，义为「装卸工；装载机」

senses.title: Take goods off
senses.definition: to remove goods or cargo from a ship, truck, or other carrier
senses.definitionCN: 把货物从船、卡车等运输工具上搬下来
senses.example: The crew unloaded the fish onto the wet harbour stones.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们把鱼卸到湿漉漉的码头石板上。
senses.why: Un- reverses and load is what was put on board: the cargo comes off, and the ship rides higher.
senses.whyCN: un- 表示反向，load 是被装上的东西：货物离船，船身也随之抬高。

senses.title: Take the bullets out
senses.definition: to remove the ammunition from a gun so that it cannot fire
senses.definitionCN: 把弹药从枪里取出，使枪不能击发
senses.example: He unloaded the rifle before handing it to the guide.
senses.exampleCN: 他把步枪里的子弹退出来，才交给向导。
senses.why: A gun is loaded like a cart, so the same verb empties it and makes it safe to pass on.
senses.whyCN: 枪和车一样会被「装上」东西，因此同一个动词让它变空、变得可以递出去。

senses.title: Put down a burden
senses.definition: to set down something heavy that one has been carrying
senses.definitionCN: 把一直扛着的重物放下来
senses.example: The porters unloaded their baskets at the top of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 搬运工在台阶顶上把筐放下。
senses.why: Here the carrier is a person, and the load is carried on the back rather than in a vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 这里的载具是人，负载扛在背上而不是装在车里。

senses.title: Tell someone your worries
senses.titleCN: 倾诉；把心里的话说出来
senses.definition: in informal speech, to tell someone all your problems or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中，把烦恼或感受全部说给别人听
senses.example: She called her sister to unload after the long meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开完那个长会，她打电话给姐姐倾诉了一番。
senses.why: Trouble behaves like freight: once it is set down on someone else, the speaker feels lighter.
senses.whyCN: 烦恼像货物一样：一旦放到别人那边，说话的人就轻了。

senses.title: Remove from a system
senses.definition: of data or software, to transfer it out or remove it from a place
senses.definitionCN: 指数据或程序，把它们转移出去或从某处移除
senses.example: The app unloads the photos to save space on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用把照片卸载出去，以节省手机空间。
senses.why: A phone or a server is the new warehouse, and its files are the freight to be moved out.
senses.whyCN: 手机或服务器成了新的仓库，里面的文件就是待搬出的货。

intro.en: Unload is the native negative prefix on load, a word that English took from the same Germanic root as lade.
intro.cn: unload 是本土否定前缀加 load，load 与 lade 同出日耳曼语词根，为英语所继承。

items.en: The verb hladan meant to draw water or to pile up goods, and gave the modern lade and load.
items.cn: 古英语动词 hladan 意为「舀水、堆货」，演变为现代的 lade 与 load。

items.en: The noun lode, meaning a load or a course, and the verb laden kept the sense of piling a burden on.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 lode 意为「负载、路线」，动词 laden 保留了「堆积重负」之意。

items.en: Un- was added to make unload, to take the burden off again, and the word covered ships, carts and guns.
items.cn: 加上 un- 构成 unload，表示把重负重新取下，用于船、车与枪。

items.en: Railways and lorries made unloading a daily industrial routine, with dockside cranes named for it.
items.cn: 铁路与卡车让卸货成为日常的工业工序，码头的吊机也以它命名。

items.en: Computers and counselling both borrowed the image: data and worries can now be unloaded too.
items.cn: 计算机与心理咨询都借用了这个意象：数据与心事如今也能「卸」出去。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in un- and load forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of removing, emptying, or confessing.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 与 load 一族的词；近义组收表示移走、清空或倾诉的动词。

entries.definition: To put goods or ammunition on; the word without the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装载」，即去掉前缀的词。

entries.definition: Adjective for a vehicle or gun with nothing in it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未装货的、未装弹的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the work of taking a load off.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卸货、卸载」。

entries.definition: To send data from a computer to a server; the opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上传」，方向相反。

entries.definition: To bring data from a network onto a device.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「下载」，从网络取到设备上。

entries.definition: To make a container have nothing in it; the result rather than the work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「倒空」，强调结果。

entries.definition: To unload cargo formally, or to release a person; used in shipping and law.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「卸货、释放」，多用于航运与法律。

entries.definition: To relieve oneself of a worry by telling someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「卸下负担、倾诉」，偏书面。

entries.definition: To tell a secret to someone you trust; quieter than unload.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吐露」，比 unload 更安静、更私密。

entries.definition: A general verb for taking something away from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「移走」，泛称从某处拿走东西。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus load structure and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 load 的朴素结构，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and load is the burden: unload is to take the burden off.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，load 是重负：unload 就是把重负取下。

normal.en: A truck is unloaded at the dock; a gun is unloaded before it is handed over.
normal.cn: 卡车在码头卸货；枪在交出之前要退出子弹。

normal.en: Upload and download move data; unload moves it out of the way.
normal.cn: upload 与 download 是搬数据；unload 是把数据挪走。

normal.en: To unload on someone can mean to tell them your troubles, or to blame them.
normal.cn: unload on someone 既可指向人倾诉，也可指把气撒到人身上。

normal.en: Unloaded and empty are close, but unload is the act.
normal.cn: unloaded 与 empty 意思接近，但 unload 是动作。

abstract.en: Picture a cart that gets lighter with every box: the word tracks the moment weight leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车每卸一箱就轻一点：这个词跟着重量离开的那一瞬间。

abstract.en: From boxes to bullets to worries, unload always means the same: take the charge out.
abstract.cn: 从货物到子弹再到心事，unload 始终是同一个意思：把「装进去的东西」拿出来。

abstract.en: A person who unloads a burden is the same image, only the cargo cannot be seen.
abstract.cn: 倾诉的人用的是同一个意象，只是货物看不见。

examples.en: Workers unloaded the truck in less than an hour.
examples.cn: 工人们不到一小时就把卡车卸完了。

examples.en: Always unload the gun before cleaning it.
examples.cn: 清洁枪支前一定要先退出子弹。

examples.en: She unloaded her worries onto her friend over dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭时她把心里的烦恼全向朋友倾诉了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的楼德」——安把楼上堆的货物一件件搬下来：卸货

root: 由否定前缀 un- 加 load（源自古英语 hladan「舀水、堆货」，与 lade 同源）构成，字面即「把装上的东西取下」；近代从船只、车辆、枪械扩展到数据与心事的「卸载」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unload all remove a charge that had been put in: goods, bullets, a heavy basket, pent-up worries, or data.
sensesIntro.cn: unload 的五个义项都在把先前装进去的东西拿出来：货物、子弹、重筐、憋着的心事，或数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the tailgate drops and boxes are carried out of the truck.
core.cn: 核心意象：后挡板放下，箱子一箱箱被搬出车厢。

branches.en: THE CARGO: goods leave the ship, truck or plane.
branches.cn: 货物线：货物离开船、卡车或飞机。

branches.en: THE AMMUNITION: bullets leave the gun so it is safe.
branches.cn: 弹药线：子弹离开枪膛，枪才安全。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: a carried basket is set down at the top of the steps.
branches.cn: 重负线：扛着的筐在台阶顶上被放下。

branches.en: THE FEELINGS: what was held inside is said out loud.
branches.cn: 情感线：憋在里面的东西被说出口。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: data is moved out to free space.
branches.cn: 系统线：数据被移出去以腾出空间。

intro.en: Unload is native on both sides: an English prefix on an English verb, with English suffixes on top.
intro.cn: unload 两边都是本土成分：英语前缀加英语动词，上面再加英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin core here; the Latin-based cousins appear only as formal near meanings.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语核心；拉丁语来源的近义词只作为正式说法列出。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「装载」倒过来。

items.example: The root names the charge being carried.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被装上的负载。
它把 load 变成 loader。

items.example: An older noun from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根上较早的名词。

items.example: The formal synonym from Latin carricare.
items.exampleCN: 源自拉丁语 carricare 的正式近义词。

definition_zh: 不寻常的；少见的；独特的；奇特的
definition_en: not happening or seen often, and therefore interesting or surprising
core_image: 一条每天都走的小路上忽然出现一只孔雀，行人都停下来看
scene: 冬天一向安静的小镇忽然来了个露天马戏团，广场上支起红白相间的帐篷。It is unusual to see a circus here in the middle of winter.
sceneCN: 这里 unusual 是「不寻常的、少见的」（第 1 个义项：不常发生）；句意为在隆冬时节在这里看到马戏团很不寻常。小路上那只不该出现的孔雀，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「不同寻常地；异常地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「不寻常、罕见」
本词去掉 un-，义为「通常的、惯常的」
由 usual 加 -ly 构成，义为「通常」

senses.title: Not often met
senses.definition: not common or frequent, so that it stands out from the ordinary run of things
senses.definitionCN: 不常见或发生不多，因而从平常的事物中凸显出来
senses.example: It is unusual for him to be late twice in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 他一周迟到两次，这很不寻常。
senses.why: Un- denies and usual is what happens as a rule: the word simply steps outside the rule.
senses.whyCN: un- 是否定，usual 是按常规发生的事：这个词只是走出那条常规。

senses.title: Different from the rest
senses.definition: not like others of its kind, often in a way that draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 不像同类中的其他个体，常以引人注意的方式不同
senses.example: She has an unusual way of arranging flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 她插花的方式与众不同。
senses.why: Here the difference is not in frequency but in shape, and people notice the shape.
senses.whyCN: 这里的差别不在频率而在样子，而人们注意到的正是样子。

senses.title: Strange enough to wonder about
senses.definition: strange enough to raise a question or a doubt
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪到会引起疑问或怀疑
senses.example: There was an unusual smell in the kitchen that morning.
senses.exampleCN: 那天早上厨房里有一股怪味。
senses.why: When the difference turns unpleasant or puzzling, the word tips over into strange.
senses.whyCN: 当这种不同变得令人不适或费解时，这个词就偏向「奇怪」。

senses.title: Not the normal amount
senses.definition: of weather, prices, or numbers: outside the normal range for that place or season
senses.definitionCN: 用于天气、价格或数字，超出该地该季节的正常范围
senses.example: Unusual heat in April dried the young plants.
senses.exampleCN: 四月反常的高温把小苗晒干了。
senses.why: What normally happens is a range, and anything outside it is marked by the word.
senses.whyCN: 「通常」其实是一个范围，走出范围的东西就被这个词标记出来。

senses.title: As a polite notice
senses.definition: in phrases such as nothing unusual, telling someone that all is well
senses.definitionCN: 在 nothing unusual 一类说法中，告诉别人一切正常
senses.example: The guard walked round the building and found nothing unusual.
senses.exampleCN: 保安绕楼走了一圈，没有发现异常。
senses.why: The word can also certify the absence of the extraordinary, which is why guards and doctors use it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能证明「没有特殊状况」，因此保安与医生都爱用它。

intro.en: Unusual is a plain English negative on usual, a word that came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: unusual 是英语在 usual 上加的否定，而 usual 经由法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Usus meant use, and the adjective usualis meant fit for use or common in practice.
items.cn: 拉丁语 usus 意为「使用」，形容词 usualis 意为「合用的、习以为常的」。

items.en: French usual kept the sense of what is customary and happens as a rule.
items.cn: 法语 usual 保留了「惯常、按常规发生」的意思。

items.en: English adopted usual for what is ordinary, and the noun use stands at its root.
items.cn: 英语以 usual 指平常之事，其词根正是表示「使用」的 use。

items.en: Un- was added to make unusual, and the word spread from habits to weather, smells, and prices.
items.cn: 加 un- 构成 unusual，这个词从习惯扩展到天气、气味与价格。

items.en: The pattern nothing unusual became the standard reassuring phrase in reports and checks.
items.cn: nothing unusual 成了报告与检查中标准的安抚说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in un- and usual forms; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what stands outside the ordinary.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 与 usual 一族的词；近义组收表示「非常态」的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning more than is normal, as in unusually warm.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「异常地」，如 unusually warm。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being rare.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不寻常」。

entries.definition: Happening as a rule; the word without the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「通常的」，即去掉否定前缀的词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in most cases.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「通常」。

entries.definition: Not able to be used; close in spelling, different in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不能用的」，形近而意义不同。

entries.definition: Not often found; it counts frequency rather than judging strangeness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稀少的」，只讲频率，不带奇怪之感。

entries.definition: Slightly strange or unexpected, often in a light way.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「古怪的」，常带轻松的口气。

entries.definition: Belonging to one thing only, or strange in a way that is hard to name.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独有的」或「说不清地古怪」。

entries.definition: Unusually good or large; it usually praises rather than puzzles.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「杰出的、异常的」，多带赞美意。

entries.definition: Far outside the ordinary, stronger and more formal than unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非凡的」，比 unusual 更强、更正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus usual structure and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 usual 的朴素结构，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and usual means as a rule: not as a rule.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，usual 表示「按常规」：不合常规。

normal.en: The pattern with a for phrase names a break in habit.
normal.cn: 带 for 短语的句型点出的是习惯被打破。

normal.en: Nothing unusual is what guards write when all is well.
normal.cn: nothing unusual 是保安在一切正常时写下的。

normal.en: Unusually warm is stronger than warm and means warmer than normal.
normal.cn: unusually warm 比 warm 更强，意为比平常更暖。

normal.en: An unusual name is one you have not heard before.
normal.cn: an unusual name 指你没听过的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a peacock on a footpath people walk every day: nothing about the path has changed, only what appears on it.
abstract.cn: 想象天天走的小路上出现一只孔雀：小路本身没变，变的只是路上出现的东西。

abstract.en: Unusual measures distance from a habit, so the same thing can be unusual in one town and ordinary in another.
abstract.cn: unusual 衡量的是与习惯的距离，所以同一件事在一个镇异常，在另一个镇平常。

abstract.en: The word is mild: it notices a difference without declaring it good or bad.
abstract.cn: 这个词语气温和：它注意到差别，却不判定好坏。

examples.en: It is unusual for the museum to close on a weekday.
examples.cn: 博物馆在工作日闭馆是不寻常的。

examples.en: The garden has an unusual shape, like a long leaf.
examples.cn: 这个花园形状独特，像一片细长的叶子。

examples.en: Nothing unusual was found during the night inspection.
examples.cn: 夜间巡查中没有发现异常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的优热」——安觉得这份优热很不寻常：不寻常的

root: 由否定前缀 un- 加 usual 构成；usual 源自拉丁语 usus「使用」所生的 usualis「合用的、习以为常的」，经古法语进入英语；unusual 由「不合习惯」扩展到罕见、独特、反常与「无异常」等说法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unusual all measure distance from a habit or a range: a rare event, a distinctive shape, a puzzling smell, weather outside its season, or the reassuring absence of any of these.
sensesIntro.cn: unusual 的五个义项都在衡量与习惯或正常范围的距离：罕见之事、与众不同的样子、令人困惑的气味、超出季节的天气，以及反过来「并无此类情况」的安抚说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a peacock standing on an everyday footpath.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只孔雀站在每天走的小路上。

branches.en: THE FREQUENCY: the event does not happen as a rule.
branches.cn: 频率线：这件事不按常规发生。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the thing differs from its kind in form.
branches.cn: 形状线：此物在形态上不同于同类。

branches.en: THE DOUBT: the difference puzzles the senses.
branches.cn: 疑惑线：这种不同让感官困惑。

branches.en: THE RANGE: weather or prices step outside the normal band.
branches.cn: 范围线：天气或价格走出正常区间。

branches.en: THE ABSENCE: the word also certifies that nothing is wrong.
branches.cn: 缺席线：这个词也能证明一切正常。

intro.en: Unusual pairs an English negative prefix with a Latin-derived adjective, so the ends are English and the middle is Latin.
intro.cn: unusual 是英语否定前缀配一个拉丁语来源的形容词，两端是英语、中间是拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun usus and the adjective usualis are both recorded, and French stands between them and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 usus 与形容词 usualis 均有记录，法语位于它们与英语之间。

items.example: The root names practice and habit.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指实践与习惯。
它把 usus 变成 usual。

items.example: The French form that reached English.

definition_zh: 在……上；一……就；依据；关于；（用于固定说法）
definition_en: on, in the sense of resting on something, and in phrases such as upon arriving, meaning as soon as
core_image: 一只手把一本书轻轻放在桌面上，书与桌面正好贴合
scene: 讲故事的人一开口就要用到这个词，只写第一句，屋里便安静下来。Once upon a time there was a miller with three sons.
sceneCN: 这里 upon 是「在……之上」，用在固定说法 once upon a time 里（第 1 个义项：在……上）；句意为从前有一位磨坊主，他有三个儿子。书放在桌面上的那种贴合，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 一……就（后接名词或动名词）

derivatives.zh: 由 there 与 upon 合成，义为「随即；因此」
由 where 与 upon 合成，义为「于是；随后」
由 here 与 upon 合成，义为「于是；就此」

senses.title: Resting on
senses.definition: on, used of something resting on a surface, in a more formal or literary tone
senses.definitionCN: 在……上面，指某物置于表面，语气更正式或更文学
senses.example: He placed the letter upon the table and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信放在桌上，离开了房间。
senses.why: Upon is the older northern form of on, and it has kept the plain sense of contact with a surface.
senses.whyCN: upon 是 on 较早的北方形式，一直保留着与表面接触的朴素意义。

senses.title: As soon as
senses.definition: immediately after, used before a noun or an -ing form
senses.definitionCN: 在……之后立即，后接名词或动名词
senses.example: Upon arriving, she asked to see the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 她一到达就要求见经理。
senses.why: To rest upon something is to touch it at once, so the word marks the exact moment of contact.
senses.whyCN: 「落在某物上」就是立即触及，因此这个词标记的是接触的那一刻。

senses.title: Depending on
senses.definition: dependent on, or according to, as in upon request or upon my word
senses.definitionCN: 取决于或根据……，如 upon request、upon my word
senses.example: The room is cleaned daily upon request.
senses.exampleCN: 一经请求，房间每日都会打扫。
senses.why: What rests upon a support depends on it, so the sense of support turns into causation and condition.
senses.whyCN: 依于支撑之物就意味着取决于它，支撑义由此转为条件与因果。

senses.title: About, concerning
senses.definition: in formal phrases such as upon this matter, meaning about it
senses.definitionCN: 在 upon this matter 一类正式说法中，意为「关于此事」
senses.example: The board will decide upon the matter next week.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会将在下周就此事作出决定。
senses.why: Attention rests on a subject in the same way a hand rests on a table.
senses.whyCN: 注意力落在某个题目上，正如手落在桌面上。

senses.title: Frozen in stories and oaths
senses.titleCN: 用于故事与誓言等固定说法
senses.definition: fixed in formulas such as once upon a time and upon my word, where on would sound plainer
senses.definitionCN: 固定于 once upon a time、upon my word 等套语中，换用 on 会显得过于平淡
senses.example: On such a night, the old song says, no one goes upon the moor.
senses.exampleCN: 那首老歌里说，在这样的夜里没人会去荒原。
senses.why: Formulas outlive ordinary speech, which is why the older word survives mostly in them.
senses.whyCN: 套语比日常言语活得更久，这个词也因此多半留在套语里。

intro.en: Upon is a northern Old English compound of up and on, which spread south and became the literary twin of on.
intro.cn: upon 是古英语里把 up 与 on 合成的北方形式，后来传到南方，成为 on 的文雅双生词。

items.en: On was the plain preposition, and the compound uppon joined up with on to stress position above.
items.cn: 古英语 on 是普通介词，复合形式 uppon 把 up 与 on 结合，强调在上方。

items.en: The form spread from the north of England, where up- compounds were common in speech.
items.cn: 这一形式从英格兰北部传播开来，那里把 up 构成的复合词在口语中很常见。

items.en: By the fourteenth century upon was used in southern writing along with on, with a more elevated ring.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，upon 与 on 一起出现在南方写作中，语气更为庄重。

items.en: Grammar left upon to set phrases such as once upon a time and to formal prose.
items.cn: 现代语法把 upon 留给 once upon a time 一类套语以及正式散文。

items.en: The as-soon-as sense settled in the pattern upon doing or upon a noun.
items.cn: 「一……就」的意思定型为 upon 加动名词或名词的句型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds on upon and words easily confused with it; the near-meaning group gathers prepositions and phrases of place and time.
note.cn: 形近组收由 upon 构成的复合词与易混词；近义组收表示地点与时间的介词与短语。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning immediately after that, or for that reason.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「随即、因此」。

entries.definition: A conjunction meaning after which, as in one act followed by another.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「于是、随后」。

entries.definition: An old adverb meaning at this point, or on this matter.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「于是、就此」。

entries.definition: The plain modern preposition; upon is its older, more formal twin.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，即现代普通形式，upon 是它更正式的旧版双生词。

entries.definition: On to, moving towards a surface; it implies motion, which upon does not.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「到……上面」，含移动义，upon 不含。

entries.definition: The plain conjunction for the first sense, followed by a full clause.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「一……就」，后接完整从句。

entries.definition: A neutral phrase for what follows at once.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「紧接着之后」，语气中性。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the sense of depending on a rule or source.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「根据」，表达依据义。

entries.definition: About a matter; the formal equivalent in the fourth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于」，对应第 4 个义项。

entries.definition: On top of; literary and rarer than upon.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……顶上」，更文学也更少见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the up-on shape behind the word and the set phrases it survives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后 up 加 on 的形状，以及它留存的固定说法。

normal.en: Upon is up plus on: resting above and touching the surface.
normal.cn: upon 是 up 加 on：在上面并与表面接触。

normal.en: Once upon a time is the oldest and most famous use of the word.
normal.cn: once upon a time 是这个词最古老也最有名的用法。

normal.en: Upon arriving means the very moment of arrival.
normal.cn: upon arriving 意为到达的那一刻。

normal.en: Upon request, upon my word: formal phrases where on would sound flat.
normal.cn: upon request、upon my word 等，换用 on 会太平淡。

normal.en: Use on in daily speech and keep upon for stories and contracts.
normal.cn: 日常说话用 on，故事与合同里保留 upon。

abstract.en: Picture a hand laying a book flat on a table: contact happens at one instant, which is why the word also means as soon as.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把书平放在桌上：接触只在那一瞬，所以这个词也有「一……就」的意思。

abstract.en: Whatever rests on a support depends on it, so place turns into condition without changing form.
abstract.cn: 凡是靠在支撑上的都取决于它，于是「位置」不变形式地转为「条件」。

abstract.en: Upon survives because stories love old words: the phrase is older than any particular tale.
abstract.cn: upon 因为故事偏爱旧词而留存：这个说法比任何具体故事都更古老。

examples.en: Once upon a time a fisherman found a key in the sand.
examples.cn: 从前有个渔夫在沙子里捡到一把钥匙。

examples.en: Upon leaving the hall, he called his mother at once.
examples.cn: 一走出大厅，他立刻给母亲打了电话。

examples.en: Doors are opened upon request by the caretaker.
examples.cn: 管理员可应请求开门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额碰」——额头一碰就把东西放上去：在……上

root: 古英语以 up 与 on 合成的北方形式 uppon，强调「在上方贴合」，后传入南方写作；现代其字面义已多由 on 承担，upon 主要留在 once upon a time 之类套语、正式散文与 upon doing 的结构中。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of upon all keep one contact: something rests on a surface, or touches it at a single instant, or depends on it, or concerns it, or survives in a story whose very first words hold it.
sensesIntro.cn: upon 的五个义项都保留同一种接触：某物落在表面上、在某一瞬间触及表面、依赖表面、涉及某个题目，或者留在一开口就用到它的故事里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand setting a book down flat on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把书平放在桌面上。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: one thing rests upon another.
branches.cn: 表面线：一样东西落在另一样上面。

branches.en: THE MOMENT: contact happens at once, so the word means as soon as.
branches.cn: 时刻线：接触立即发生，所以表示「一……就」。

branches.en: THE SUPPORT: what rests on something depends on it.
branches.cn: 支撑线：靠在上面的就取决于它。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: attention rests on a matter under discussion.
branches.cn: 题目线：注意力落在正在讨论的事情上。

branches.en: THE FORMULA: the oldest phrases keep the oldest word.
branches.cn: 套语线：最老的套语留住最老的词。

intro.en: Upon is not built with affixes but with two prepositions joined; its later family adds there, where, and here.
intro.cn: upon 不是用词缀构成，而是两个介词组合；后来这一族又加了 there、where、here。

latinIntro.en: The word is wholly Germanic; the Latin-based near meanings are listed only because students often confuse them.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全是日耳曼语来源；列出拉丁语来源的近义词只因学生常混淆。

items.example: It adds the sense of position above.
The older spelling of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词较早的拼写。

items.example: A look-alike with motion built in.

definition_zh: 更新；使现代化；向……提供最新消息；更新；最新消息
definition_en: to make something more modern or bring it up to date, or a report with the newest facts
core_image: 一册日历被逐页翻到最新一天，旧的一页被撕下，新的数字露出来
scene: 手机在夜里弹出提示，说系统需要重启才能装上新版本。The app asks you to update it before the new features can be used.
sceneCN: 这里 update 是「更新」（第 1 个义项：使内容变为最新的）；句意为这个应用要求你先更新，之后才能使用新功能。日历被翻到最新那一页，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 更新；最新消息；最新版本

collocations.zh: 向某人通报……的最新情况

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「已更新的；最新的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「更新过程」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「更新程序；更新者」
由本词的两个部件加连字符构成，义为「最新的」

senses.title: Make it current
senses.definition: to change something so that it contains the newest information or works in the newest way
senses.definitionCN: 改动某物，使其包含最新的信息或以最新的方式工作
senses.example: She updates the price list every Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周一早上更新价目表。
senses.why: Up brings the thing to the present, and date names that present: the record is lifted to today.
senses.whyCN: up 把东西提到当下，date 指这个当下：记录被抬到了今天。

senses.title: Tell someone the news
senses.definition: to give someone the latest facts about a situation
senses.definitionCN: 把某一情况的最新事实告诉某人
senses.example: The officer updated the family on the search every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 警官每天晚上向这家人通报搜寻的进展。
senses.why: The same lifting happens in words instead of records: the listener is brought up to the current state of affairs.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「抬高」发生在消息而非记录上：听者被带到事情的当前状态。

senses.title: A newer version
senses.definition: a new version of a program, file, or document that replaces the old one
senses.definitionCN: 取代旧版本的程序、文件或文档的新版本
senses.example: The update fixed a fault that closed the program without warning.
senses.exampleCN: 这次更新修复了一个会让程序毫无预兆关闭的故障。
senses.why: The verb turns into a countable noun, so each act of bringing something current becomes a thing you can install.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为可数名词，于是每一次「带到当下」都成了可以安装的东西。

senses.title: A short news report
senses.definition: a short piece of news giving the newest facts about a running story
senses.definitionCN: 关于进行中的事件的最新事实的简短报道
senses.example: We will bring you an update at nine o'clock.
senses.exampleCN: 我们将在九点为您带来最新报道。
senses.why: News is a story that keeps moving, so it needs the same word: a short report that catches the audience up.
senses.whyCN: 新闻是不断变动的事件，因此需要同一个词：一则把听众带到最新进展的短报道。

senses.title: Bring something up to standard
senses.definition: to modernize a building, system, or machine so that it meets present needs
senses.definitionCN: 对建筑、系统或机器进行现代化改造，使其满足当下需要
senses.example: The library was updated with new lights and faster computers.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆翻新了照明，换上了更快的电脑。
senses.why: Here the standard being reached is not a date but the present day itself: an old building is brought up to how people live now.
senses.whyCN: 这里要达到的标准不是某个日期，而是当下本身：旧建筑被提到人们今天生活的方式。

intro.en: Update is a modern compound: the English adverb up joined to the French-derived verb date.
intro.cn: update 是近代复合词：英语副词 up 加源自法语的动词 date。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and the Latin phrase data, items given, became the source of date in the sense of a written day.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dare 意为「给予」，短语 data（给予之物）成为 date 指「日期」的来源。

items.en: French date named the day on which a document is given or made.
items.cn: 古法语 date 指文件签发或写成的日期。

items.en: English took date for the day of writing, and later used the verb date for marking a time.
items.cn: 英语以 date 指写作日期，后来动词 date 表示标注时间。

items.en: Up and date were combined in the twentieth century, first for keeping records current.
items.cn: 二十世纪把 up 与 date 合成，最初用于使记录保持最新。

items.en: Computers made update a household word, as patches and news feeds both began to update themselves.
items.cn: 计算机让 update 家喻户晓，补丁与新闻推送都开始自我更新。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with up and date; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of renewal and news with different scopes.
note.cn: 形近组收由 up 与 date 构成的词；近义组收表示更新与通报的动词，范围不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning current, keeping the newest facts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最新的」，保持最新信息。

entries.definition: No longer current, old enough to be replaced.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过时的」，旧到该被替换。

entries.definition: A day of the month, or a meeting with someone romantically.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「日期」，也可指约会。

entries.definition: Adjective for something already made current.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已更新的」。

entries.definition: To send data to a server; it shares the prefix, not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上传」，只共享前缀。

entries.definition: To raise something to a higher grade or better model.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「升级」，把某物提到更高等级或更好的型号。

entries.definition: To make valid again, or to begin again after a break.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「续期、更新」，使重新有效或重新开始。

entries.definition: To bring an old building or system up to present standards.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「现代化」，把旧建筑或系统提到当下标准。

entries.definition: To change a text or a plan after looking at it again.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修订」，重看后加以改动。

entries.definition: To make something feel or look new again, or to reload a screen.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使恢复、刷新」，包括刷新屏幕。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the up plus date structure and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 up 加 date 的结构，以及这个词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Up means to a higher level and date means the day: bring it up to today.
normal.cn: up 表示「向上」，date 表示「日期」：把它提到今天。

normal.en: A software update replaces the old version quietly at night.
normal.cn: 软件更新在夜里悄悄替换旧版本。

normal.en: Update someone on a matter means telling them the latest facts.
normal.cn: 向某人通报某事的最新情况，用的就是 update。

normal.en: Up-to-date is the adjective, outdated is the opposite.
normal.cn: up-to-date 是形容词，outdated 是它的反面。

normal.en: The noun update in British English puts the stress on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 名词 update 在英式英语中重音前移到第一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar page torn away: the word is about the difference between what is written and what is true now.
abstract.cn: 想象日历被撕下一页：这个词说的是「写着的」与「此刻为真的」之间的差距。

abstract.en: Nothing is updated once for ever; the word implies a clock that keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 没有东西能更新一次就永远有效：这个词暗含一只一直在走的钟。

abstract.en: The same word serves a file and a worried family, because both need the newest facts.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既用于文件也用于焦急的家人，因为两者都需要最新的事实。

examples.en: Please update your address in the school records.
examples.cn: 请在学校记录里更新你的地址。

examples.en: The manager updated us on the new schedule by email.
examples.cn: 经理通过邮件向我们通报了新日程。

examples.en: A small update will fix the problem with the printer.
examples.cn: 一次小的更新就能修好打印机的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普戴特」——阿普把日期戴特到最新一天：更新

root: 由英语副词 up（向上、达到）与 date（源自拉丁语 dare「给予」，经古法语 date「签发日期」入英语）合成，二十世纪出现，最初指使记录保持最新，计算机时代扩展为软件更新与新闻快报。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of update all close a gap between what is written and what is true now: a list, a family waiting for news, a program, a broadcast, or a whole building.
sensesIntro.cn: update 的五个义项都在弥合「写着的」与「此刻为真的」之间的差距：一份清单、等待消息的家人、一个程序、一则快报，或一整栋建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the calendar is turned to the newest day and the old page is torn off.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历被翻到最新的一天，旧页被撕下。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a list or file is brought to the present.
branches.cn: 记录线：清单或文件被带到当下。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: someone is told the latest facts.
branches.cn: 人群线：有人被告诉最新的事实。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM: a new version replaces the old one.
branches.cn: 程序线：新版本取代旧版本。

branches.en: THE NEWS: a short report on a moving story.
branches.cn: 新闻线：关于进行中事件的简短报道。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: lights and machines are made modern.
branches.cn: 建筑线：照明与设备被现代化。

intro.en: Update is two English words joined; only the second half carries a French and Latin history.
intro.cn: update 是两个英语词组合而成；只有后半部分带有法语与拉丁语的历史。

latinIntro.en: Dare is recorded Latin, and data is its plural participle; French date stands between them and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare 有记录，data 是其分词复数；法语 date 位于它们与英语之间。

items.example: The prefix means brought up to a standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示被提到某个标准。

The French form that reached English.

definition_zh: 在楼上；往楼上；楼上的；楼上（楼层）
definition_en: on or to a higher floor of a building, or the floor or part of the building above
core_image: 一段木楼梯从门厅盘旋而上，尽头是一扇透着灯光的房门
scene: 夜里楼下还亮着灯，孩子的房间在二层，母亲轻轻敲了敲楼梯扶手。The children are already upstairs, reading in bed.
sceneCN: 这里 upstairs 是「在楼上」（第 1 个义项：位于更高的楼层）；句意为孩子们已经上楼，在床上看书。从门厅盘旋而上的那段楼梯，就是这个词的样子。

forms.label: 无变化（副词、形容词与名词）

derivatives.zh: 由 down 与 stairs 合成，义为「在楼下、往楼下」
由 up 与 stair 合成，义为「楼上的一间」（少见）
本词的后半，义为「一级楼梯」
由 stair 与 case 合成，义为「楼梯段；楼梯间」

senses.title: On a higher floor
senses.definition: on or towards a higher floor of a building, usually used after a verb of movement
senses.definitionCN: 在或朝建筑的更高楼层，通常跟在表示移动的动词之后
senses.example: She went upstairs to fetch her coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她上楼去取外套。
senses.why: Up gives the direction and stairs give the means: the word simply says the person has gone up the steps.
senses.whyCN: up 给出方向，stairs 给出途径：这个词只说明人顺着台阶上去了。

senses.title: Of a higher floor
senses.definition: living on or belonging to the floor above, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 住在或属于上面那一层，用在名词之前
senses.example: The upstairs windows were still bright at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 半夜里楼上的窗子还亮着。
senses.why: Placed before a noun, the same two pieces stop describing a movement and start labelling a thing by its floor.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，同样的两个部件不再描述动作，而是按楼层给事物贴标签。

senses.title: The upper floor itself
senses.definition: the upper floor or floors of a house, taken as a part of it
senses.definitionCN: 房屋上面的那一层或几层，被视为房子的一部分
senses.example: The upstairs of the old house had low beams and a sloping floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子的楼上有低矮的横梁和倾斜的地板。
senses.why: With the article, the phrase becomes a noun: the staircase direction turns into a named part of the house.
senses.whyCN: 加上冠词后，这个短语成了名词：上楼的方向变成了房子中被命名的一部分。

senses.title: In a raised position
senses.definition: figuratively, in a higher or more powerful position in an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指在组织内处于更高、更有权力的位置
senses.example: After the promotion he moved upstairs into an office with a view.
senses.exampleCN: 升职之后他搬到了楼上，进了一间能看到风景的办公室。
senses.why: Buildings stack rank as they stack floors, so going up the stairs becomes a picture of gaining authority.
senses.whyCN: 建筑在叠楼层的同时也叠等级，于是上楼成了获得权力的画面。

senses.title: A step up in price
senses.definition: in set phrases such as the man upstairs, meaning a leader or the boss
senses.definitionCN: 在 the man upstairs 一类说法中，指上级或老板
senses.example: The men upstairs want the report by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 上面那几位要这份报告在周五前交。
senses.why: The people on the floor above become a nickname for the people who decide, since power sits higher in the building.
senses.whyCN: 楼上那层的人成了决策者的绰号，因为在楼里权力总是坐得更高。

intro.en: Upstairs joins two native English words: the adverb up and the noun stair or stairs.
intro.cn: upstairs 把两个英语本土词合在一起：副词 up 与名词 stair 或 stairs。

items.en: Up is a native adverb of Old English meaning upwards or above.
items.cn: up 是古英语中表示「向上、在上」的本土副词。

items.en: Stǣger meant a stair or a flight of stairs, and became the modern stair and stairs.
items.cn: 古英语 stǣger 意为「一级楼梯或一段楼梯」，演变为现代的 stair 与 stairs。

items.en: The two were written as up staires, a phrase telling where a person moved in a house.
items.cn: 二者起初写作 up staires，是一个说明人在屋中往哪儿去的短语。

items.en: The compound settled as one word, and the noun use followed for the upper floor itself.
items.cn: 这个复合词定型为一个词，随后又作名词指楼层本身。

items.en: Idiomatic uses spread, from the man upstairs to the informal saying that someone has gone upstairs.
items.cn: 各种惯用说法流行开来，从 the man upstairs 到说某人「上了楼」的俗语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with up and stair; the near-meaning group gathers words for floors and parts of a house.
note.cn: 形近组收含 up 与 stair 的词；近义组收表示楼层与房屋部分的词。

entries.definition: On or to a lower floor; the direct opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在楼下、往楼下」，正好相反。

entries.definition: An older adjective for a single upper room; now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「楼上房间的」，较古老且少见。

entries.definition: A person who has risen quickly in rank and acts above their place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴发户、自命不凡的新贵」，形近而意义不同。

entries.definition: The whole structure of steps and rails between floors.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「楼梯」，指整段楼梯结构。

entries.definition: A flight of stairs, sometimes outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「楼梯、阶梯」，有时指室外阶梯。

entries.definition: Higher than, in space, without naming a floor.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在上方」，不指明楼层。

entries.definition: Directly above one's head, often in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上」，多指露天环境。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for the storey above ground level.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「上层楼面」，指地面层之上的楼层。

entries.definition: The highest storey of a building, usually one only.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「顶层」，通常只有一层。

entries.definition: Towards a higher place or level; about direction, not floors.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「向上」，指方向而非楼层。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two plain pieces, up and stairs, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个朴素部件 up 与 stairs，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Up plus stairs: where the steps lead.
normal.cn: up 加 stairs：台阶通向的地方。

normal.en: Go upstairs after the verb; the upstairs window before the noun.
normal.cn: go upstairs 放在动词之后；the upstairs window 放在名词之前。

normal.en: Downstairs is the mirror image, one letter of direction changed.
normal.cn: downstairs 是镜像，只改了方向那一个字。

normal.en: The man upstairs is an old joke for the boss on the floor above.
normal.cn: the man upstairs 是称楼上老板的老笑话。

normal.en: The upstairs of a house is the upper part taken as a whole.
normal.cn: 房子的楼上部分整体称作 the upstairs。

abstract.en: Picture a light at the end of a wooden staircase: the word points up to where someone is still awake.
abstract.cn: 想象木楼梯尽头还亮着灯：这个词指的是有人还没睡的那个上面。

abstract.en: Floors carry rank, so moving upstairs can mean being given more power rather than a better room.
abstract.cn: 楼层承载等级，因此搬到楼上可能意味着给了更多权力，而不是更好的房间。

abstract.en: The word is plain and local: it measures a house, not a skyline.
abstract.cn: 这个词朴素而局部：它量的是房子，不是天际线。

examples.en: He carried the suitcase upstairs and set it by the bed.
examples.cn: 他把行李搬上楼，放在床边。

examples.en: The upstairs room is quiet, but it gets very hot in summer.
examples.cn: 楼上的房间很安静，但夏天非常热。

examples.en: We could hear footsteps on the stairs upstairs.
examples.cn: 我们能听见楼上楼梯上的脚步声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普斯泰尔」——阿普顺着台阶斯泰尔上去：在楼上

root: 由古英语副词 up（向上）与名词 stǣger（今 stair、stairs）合成，中古英语作 up staires，后定型为一个词，既作副词也作形容词与名词，与 downstairs 相对。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of upstairs all point to the higher part of a building: a movement, a window, a whole floor, a place of authority, or the boss who sits there.
sensesIntro.cn: upstairs 的五个义项都指向建筑中较高的部分：一次上楼的动作、一扇窗、整层楼、有权力的位置，或坐在那里的上级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden staircase winding up to a lit doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：木楼梯盘旋而上，通到一扇亮着灯的门口。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT: one goes upstairs with something in hand.
branches.cn: 动作线：手里拿着东西上楼。

branches.en: THE WINDOWS: the upstairs windows belong to the floor above.
branches.cn: 窗户线：楼上的窗属于上面那一层。

branches.en: THE PART: the upstairs is a part of the whole house.
branches.cn: 部分线：the upstairs 是整座房子的一部分。

branches.en: THE RANK: to move upstairs is to rise in an organisation.
branches.cn: 等级线：搬到楼上就是在组织里升了一层。

branches.en: THE BOSS: the people upstairs decide things.
branches.cn: 上司线：上面那些人做决定。

intro.en: Upstairs has no affixes: it is two native words side by side, with the plural -s on stairs.
intro.cn: upstairs 没有词缀：两个本土词并排，只有 stairs 词尾的复数 -s。

latinIntro.en: No Latin here; the table lists the Latin-based near meanings only for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；表内只列出拉丁语来源的近义词作对照。

items.meaning: a step, a flight of steps

items.exampleCN: 它构成 upstart 与 upward。

items.example: A cousin that names the structure.
It appears in the Latin-based synonym overhead.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在拉丁语来源的近义词中。

definition_zh: 向上的；上升的；向高处；向上
definition_en: moving or pointing towards a higher place or level, or an increase in amount
core_image: 一片叶子从地面被风托起，沿着一条斜向的天空曲线一路升高
scene: 报表摊在桌上，销售曲线从左下角一点点爬向右上角，经理用手指沿着它划过。The sales figures have been on an upward trend all year.
sceneCN: 这里 upward 是「上升的」（第 1 个义项：朝更高的地方或水平）；句意为全年销售数字一直呈上升趋势。被风托起、一路升高的叶片，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -s 构成，英式英语里作副词用，义为「向上」
由本词加 -s 与 of 构成，义为「……以上」
由 down 与 -ward 构成，义为「向下的」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「向上地」，如 upwardly mobile

senses.title: Towards a higher place
senses.definition: moving or pointing towards a higher position, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高位置移动或指向，通常用在名词前
senses.example: He gave a quick upward glance at the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝天花板飞快地向上看了一眼。
senses.why: Up supplies the height and the old suffix -ward supplies the direction: a look turned towards what is above.
senses.whyCN: up 提供高度，古老后缀 -ward 提供方向：一道转向上面之物的目光。

senses.title: In an upward direction
senses.definition: towards a higher place, used after a verb of movement
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的地方，放在表示移动的动词之后
senses.example: The kite climbed upward until it was only a dot.
senses.exampleCN: 风筝一直向上飞，直到只成了一个小点。
senses.why: After a verb of movement the same word stops naming a direction and starts tracing the path taken.
senses.whyCN: 放在移动动词之后，同一个词不再命名方向，而是描出走过的路径。

senses.title: Rising in amount
senses.definition: of prices, numbers, or costs: increasing over a period
senses.definitionCN: 用于价格、数字或成本，指在一段时间里不断增加
senses.example: There has been upward pressure on wages since the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 入春以来工资一直承受着上涨压力。
senses.why: A line on a chart moves like a kite in the sky, so a rise in numbers borrows the language of height.
senses.whyCN: 图上的线像天空中的风筝一样移动，于是数字的上涨借用了高度的话。

senses.title: A climb in position
senses.definition: moving towards a higher social or working position
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的社会或职业位置移动
senses.example: The family was described as upwardly mobile in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 调查中把这家人描述为地位正在上升的家庭。
senses.why: Society is imagined as a ladder, and anyone climbing it is moving in the same direction the word names.
senses.whyCN: 社会被想象成一把梯子，往上爬的人正朝这个词所指的方向移动。

senses.title: More than a stated figure
senses.definition: in the British phrase upwards of, meaning more than a given number
senses.definitionCN: 英式说法 upwards of 意为「超过某一数目」
senses.example: Upwards of two hundred people came to the opening.
senses.exampleCN: 开幕那天来了两百多人。
senses.why: On a scale, going upward from a number means passing it: the spatial word becomes a way of saying slightly more.
senses.whyCN: 在刻度上从某个数往上走就是越过它：空间词于是成了「略多于」的说法。

intro.en: Upward is a native compound of up and an old suffix meaning turned towards.
intro.cn: upward 是本土复合词，由 up 加一个意为「朝向」的古老后缀构成。

items.en: Up is a native adverb for upwards, and the suffix -weard meant turned in the direction of.
items.cn: up 是表示向上的本土副词，后缀 -weard 意为「朝向某个方向」。

items.en: The compound upweard was formed on the same pattern as hāmweard, homeward.
items.cn: 复合词 upweard 与 hāmweard（朝家）按同一方式构成。

items.en: The ending softened to -ward, giving upward, alongside such words as forward and downward.
items.cn: 词尾软化为 -ward，形成 upward，与 forward、downward 并列。

items.en: The form upwards became usual as an adverb in Britain, while American usage mostly keeps upward.
items.cn: 副词形式 upwards 在英式英语中常用，而美式英语多半保留 upward。

items.en: Commerce gave the word its figurative life in upward trend and upward pressure.
items.cn: 商业让这个词在上升趋势与上涨压力等说法里有了比喻生命。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in up and -ward; the near-meaning group gathers words for rising, in space or in numbers.
note.cn: 形近组收含 up 与 -ward 的词；近义组收表示在空间或数字上上升的词。

entries.definition: The British adverb form; upwards of means more than.
entries.definitionCN: 英式副词形式；upwards of 意为「……以上」。

entries.definition: Towards a lower place; the direct opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「向下的」，正好相反。

entries.definition: Towards the front; built with the same old suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「向前的」，用的是同一后缀。

entries.definition: Someone who has risen quickly and acts above their place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴发户」，形近而意义不同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a rising way, as in upwardly mobile.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向上地」，如 upwardly mobile。

entries.definition: Going up, often of prices or the sun; plainer than upward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上升的」，多用于价格或太阳，比 upward 更朴素。

entries.definition: Going upwards in order or height; technical and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上升的、递增的」，较正式且多用于技术语境。

entries.definition: Moving up by effort, as a plant or a price.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「攀升的」，指需用力向上，如藤蔓或价格。

entries.definition: Becoming larger in number or amount, with no direction in space.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不断增加的」，只讲数量不讲方向。

entries.definition: The comparative of high; compares two levels rather than showing motion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「更高的」，比较两个水平而非表示动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two pieces, up and the old suffix for direction, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个部件 up 与表示方向的古老后缀，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Up plus ward, meaning turned towards: turned upwards.
normal.cn: up 加 ward，意为「朝向」：朝向上方。

normal.en: Upward trend and upward pressure are the two common business uses.
normal.cn: upward trend 与 upward pressure 是两个常见的商业用法。

normal.en: British English prefers upwards as an adverb, American keeps upward.
normal.cn: 英式英语副词多用 upwards，美式保留 upward。

normal.en: Upwards of two hundred means more than two hundred.
normal.cn: upwards of two hundred 意为两百多。

normal.en: Downward is the mirror image with one word changed.
normal.cn: downward 只换了一个词，正好相反。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf lifted by the wind: the word traces the line from the ground to the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一片被风托起的叶子：这个词画出从地面到天空的那条线。

abstract.en: In graphs the word becomes a slope, and a slope can be read in one glance.
abstract.cn: 在图表里这个词变成一条斜线，一眼就能读懂。

abstract.en: Every upward trend is only a direction for a time; the word makes no promise that it lasts.
abstract.cn: 每个上升趋势都只是一时的方向：这个词并不保证它会持续。

examples.en: He pointed upward at the birds circling the tower.
examples.cn: 他向上指着在塔边盘旋的鸟。

examples.en: The company reports an upward trend in sales this year.
examples.cn: 公司报告今年销售呈上升趋势。

examples.en: Upwards of fifty students joined the reading club.
examples.cn: 五十多名学生加入了读书会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普沃德」——阿普一路向上走往沃德：向上的

root: 由古英语副词 up（向上）加表方向的后缀 -weard（朝向）构成 upweard，与 hāmweard、forward 同型；词尾后软化为 -ward，英式副词形作 upwards，近代又生出上升趋势、上涨压力等比喻用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of upward all give a direction: a glance at the ceiling, a kite climbing, prices rising, a family moving up, or a number slightly exceeded.
sensesIntro.cn: upward 的五个义项都给出一个方向：抬头看天花板、风筝升空、物价上涨、家世上升，或略超某个数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf lifted by the wind, climbing on a line into the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被风托起的叶子，沿一条线升向天空。

branches.en: THE LOOK: an upward glance goes to the ceiling.
branches.cn: 视线线：向上的一瞥看向天花板。

branches.en: THE MOTION: after a verb of movement the word gives direction.
branches.cn: 动作线：放在移动动词之后给出方向。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: prices and costs move upward on a chart.
branches.cn: 数字线：价格与成本在图上向上移动。

branches.en: THE RANK: a family moves upward in society.
branches.cn: 等级线：一个家庭在社会中向上移动。

branches.en: THE COUNT: upwards of a number is a little more than it.
branches.cn: 计数线：upwards of 某数意为略多于该数。

intro.en: Upward is a native word plus an old Germanic suffix, and English adds -s and -ly on top.
intro.cn: upward 是本土词加古老的日耳曼语后缀，英语上面再加 -s 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin in the word; Latin-based near meanings are listed only for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁成分；拉丁语来源的近义词只作对照列出。

items.example: The suffix turns it into a direction word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把它变成方向词。
